Span: Mar 2005–Jun 2008; documented record to Aug 24, 2011.
Anchors (slice-attributed): DS9 — EFTA00231917 (1,120 pp
probable-cause affidavit, Case #05-368), EFTA00058429,
EFTA00077923, EFTA00240536, EFTA00227381 (2,265 pp case file),
EFTA00193199 (Jun 2008 prosecutor emails), EFTA00039421;
DS1–8 — EFTA00007157, EFTA00009448, EFTA00009016, plus
EFTA00009478, EFTA00009502, EFTA00009440, EFTA00009512
(May 15, 2007 grand-jury testimony), EFTA00007253; HO — 8514,
8898, 8461, 11085, 2152, 6027, plus 1690–1693, 2150, 2148, 8614.
Endpoint: 2008 non-prosecution agreement / state plea
(HO stopping point Jun 30, 2008, HO 6027). Caveat: the signed
NPA text itself was not re-verified in the DS9 sweep; the
endpoint rests on the June 2008 negotiation emails + case file,

Links: 2 (breach), P1 (CVRA), P14 (Ruemmler counsel), P2

v2.0 DS8 extension: the plea hearing itself — certified transcript
of the June 30, 2008 plea conference (EFTA00027591); Nov 21, 2005
sworn statement of the Palm Beach house manager (EFTA00029390);
Aug 22, 2006 interview of a former residence employee, resurfaced
via Oct 4, 2021 email (EFTA00029223); 1B4 evidence-box log, last
inventoried Jul 20, 2021 (EFTA00029907); the NPA instrument itself
(EFTA00013680) and the state plea form (EFTA00013890); plea-hearing
transcript (EFTA00032238) — its cover/body show Jun 20 vs Jun 30,
2008; RESOLVED in v3.0 (WS5): the plea hearing was Jun 30, 2008 — both
copies' cover pages give Jun 30, corroborated by EFTA00013678 (plea
reported the afternoon of Jun 30) and EFTA00010507 (Marra opinion:
plea entered Jun 30, 2008). Jun 20 appears only in the transcript's
own page-2 preamble and is an internal error in the document, not a
second hearing date. A DS11 copy (EFTA02729757, 51 pp.) shows the
same cover/body discrepancy.

(21 pp.) and EFTA02725847 (11 pp.) — the negotiated plea terms
sheet (two DS11 copies of the same form). EFTA02725185 (Nov 2009,
2 pp. — AUSA letter, the USAO's account of the Rothstein fraud as
it touched the Epstein cases; the AUSA's characterizations, labeled
as such; also a Story 6 extension).

v3.2 (WS5) extension — OCR-tolerant sweep legs: EFTA00186672 (DS9): grand-jury subpoena to JEGE Inc, 103 Foulk Road, Wilmington, DE, FGJ 05-02 (2005), subpoena to testify before the grand jury. Found via the CARBYNE group ("Carbine" hit is aircraft-registration OCR noise); the subpoena itself is a 2005 grand-jury item not in Story 1's anchors. EFTA00186947 (DS9): subpoena to testify before the grand jury, to the Custodian of Records, Broward Center for the Performing Arts, 201 SW Fifth Avenue, Fort Lauderdale (2007). EFTA00279466 (DS9): PBPD evidence inventory (CDs, phone messages, digital photos; case 05-368). A single inventory list; adds the evidence-handling detail to Story 1.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — negotiation chronology, filing record, and the record to Aug 2011: the NPA's signing mechanics and signature-page questions are documented to Feb 2010, and the documented record now runs to Aug 24, 2011 (SDFL office-wide recusal) via the timeline exhibit. Sep 24, 2007 — the signing-day transmission: AUSA transmits "The final Epstein agreement (I hope)" (EFTA00215028), appeals having reviewed the first "It appearing" paragraph, signed copy by fax, originals by FedEx. The negotiation chronology is indexed in "In Re Operation Leap Year Key Correspondence Volume 1 of 2 (Through Signing of NPA) INDEX" (EFTA00190101) — tab-level chronology Nov 16, 2006–Sep 24, 2007 (Vol 1, tabs 1–81) and post-signing (Vol 2), incl. the Jul 26, 2007 USAO defense summary of terms, Sep 10 Lefcourt's first proposed NPA, Sep 11 Acosta edits, Sep 12 Lefkowitz rejecting a maritime-assault plea, Sep 14 Acosta summary (plead to an Information: 1 count obstruction + 1 count simple assault), Sep 18 Lefkowitz's §1512(d) proposal and 12-month + community-control ask, Sep 19 Lefkowitz redline (waive PSI, binding sentencing recommendation, jointly recommend an incorrect Guidelines calculation, state-court Trust, plead to "coercing a person to become a prostitute", remove appeal waiver), Sep 21 registration dispute, Sep 23 defense admission of a "mistaken assumption" behind the 796.03 plea, Sep 24 final edits 1:54 p.m., signed agreement 4:26 p.m. The index is a finding aid, not the underlying letters — cite as the index's record of the correspondence. Sep 21, 2007 — Epstein "has agreed to all the terms, including pleading to the indictment, 18 months incarceration, followed by 1 year house arrest, as a condition of 5 years probation… plus a fund for the victims as Feds require. The sticking point is requiring a plea to a registerable offense" (EFTA00215169); same file: AUSA to Krischer — deadline of tomorrow afternoon for a signed agreement "or I need to indict the case on Tuesday"; defense "only want to plead to state charges, not concurrent state and federal". Sep 18, 2007 — "I know that the U.S. Attorney will not go below 18 months of prison/jail time" (EFTA00215281); Lefkowitz's alternative: one count of §1512, 12 months + 1 year home detention, then 2 years state probation. Sep 7, 2007 — AUSA circulates both drafts, "OLY_Plea_Agreement.wpd" + "OLY_Non-Prosecution_Agreement.wpd" (EFTA00013495). Sep 10, 2007 — AUSA → Lefcourt attaching the Office's written counterproposal (EFTA00067241). Jun 23, 2008 DOJ letter (Senior Associate Deputy AG) to Lefkowitz/Starr — DOJ completed "a thorough review of the U.S. Attorney's handling"; "we see nothing in the conduct of the U.S. Attorney's Office that gives us any reason to alter our opinion"; federal prosecution "appropriate" (EFTA00179250, which also carries the Dec 5, 2008 Acosta work-release notice to Brad Edwards — USAO learned of the work-release application only after Epstein had begun it, "more than six weeks after he began participating" — and the Nov 2, 2010 CVRA litigation-hold letter). Dec 4, 2007 — Acosta's reply to Starr's Nov 28, 2007 letter (EFTA00190007): the NPA's three federal interests — (1) plead guilty to a "registerable" offense, (2) binding recommendation for a sufficient term of imprisonment, (3) not harm victims' interests — "place the victims in the same position as they would have been, had Mr. Epstein been convicted at trial. No more; no less"; "the language of Paragraph 8 was [provided] to us by defense counsel." Feb 16–17, 2010 — "We have 'umpteen' copies of the NPA, but cannot find any that contain that signature to either the Non-Prosecution Agreement or the Addendum" (EFTA00213342); the signed addendum is transmitted separately (EFTA00207077, file dated Oct 30, 2007; the Second Addendum's recital says Oct 29, 2007 — both dates recorded as written, not reconciled). Jun 27, 2008 — Acosta → Goldberger/Black: the proposed state plea "does not comply with the terms of the Non-Prosecution Agreement" (18 months community control vs the NPA's consecutive 12 + 6 months county jail "without probation or community control in lieu of imprisonment") (EFTA00067456). Jul 8, 2008 — Acosta → Goldberger: on Jun 30, 2008 USAO provided a list of 31 individuals "whom it was prepared to name in an Indictment as victims"; Jul 7, another victim identified = 32 total; victim notifications to go out Jul 9, 2008 (EFTA00067249). Jul 9, 2008 — Goldberger → AUSA: objections to the victim notification (no hand service; no redacted list; eliminate the "acknowledgment" section; add the prior representation that the government is not vouching for any claim's veracity) (EFTA00067468). Jul 1, 2008 — AUSA attaches "the agreement, with addenda, for filing with the Court under seal" + flags "misstatements" during the change of plea (Florida Science Foundation incorporated Nov 2007, not "a couple of years ago"; its "office" address is Goldberger's suite) (EFTA00013914). Aug 12, 2008 — "It looks like they only filed the original September agreement not either of the addenda" (EFTA00013965). Sep 17, 2008 — AUSA → Krischer: the NPA's confidentiality provision "requires us to inform Mr. Epstein's counsel before making any disclosure — even a compulsory disclosure" (EFTA00014172). Nov 1, 2007 — DRAFT email to the State Attorney's Office: simultaneous plea + sentencing in Oct (later Nov), self-surrender by Jan 4, 2008 (EFTA00013523 — a draft, not a sent letter). The "EPSTEIN INVESTIGATION TIMELINE" exhibit (EFTA00224943, 51 pp., 6(e) material) — dated chronology May 1, 2006–Aug 24, 2011: May 1, 2006 Reiter letter; May 23, 2006 Operation Leap Year file opening; Aug 2, 2006 subpoenas; Nov 13, 2006 subpoenas to pilots; Jun 12, 2009 Marra hearing transcript; Sep 1, 2009 draft breach letter; Sep 29, 2009 letter re Epstein violating his no-contact order on Sep 16, 2009; Oct 29, 2009 "Open file and request USAO# (2009R02690, Operation Stolen Globe)"; Jul 1–31, 2010 Epstein completed house arrest; Sep 8, 2010 administrative order closing case; Mar 20, 2011 Acosta letter; Aug 2011 SDFL office-wide recusal notices (Jul 28–Aug 29, 2011). The CVRA exhibit "JEFFREY EPSTEIN Timeline-Summary" (EFTA00192978, 5 pp.) — meetings Feb 20, Jun 26, Jul 26, Sep 7, Sep 12, 2007; Sep 24, 2007 NPA signed; Sep 25, 2007 scheduled date for federal indictment; Oct 29, 2007 deadline for plea/sentencing; Jan 4, 2008 scheduled self-surrender; plus a Federal Sentencing Guidelines calculation (§§1591, 2422(b), 2423(b); offense level 36; advisory range 188–235 months) for the contemplated federal charges. Defense-side summaries — cite ONLY as Epstein's counsel's account, not as findings: EFTA00314859 ("SUMMARY": Mar 2005 PBPD investigation; the SAO prosecutor quoted as stating there were "no real victims"; the claim "the government agreed that there had never been an underage girl on Mr. Epstein's planes") and EFTA00731146 ("SUMMARY OF MISCONDUCT ISSUES": the defense's misconduct complaint against the USAO). FBI interview notes, PBPD-side account (speaker not identified in the text layer): Epstein donated $40,000 for a machine to help PBPD review security footage and wrote a $90,000 check for a fingerprint machine (not cashed) — "around the same time that the first victim had come forward" (EFTA00153737). Dec 3, 2008 — FBI Legal Attaché (Canberra) → Australian Federal Police: USAO West Palm Beach requests AFP assistance delivering a letter to an Australian-based victim referencing the NPA outcome + terms (EFTA00269841). Mar 11, 2011 — FBI EC: Mar 9, 2011 interview at USAO Fort Lauderdale with a victim + attorneys + private investigator; she "is willing to cooperate fully with any FBI investigation involving JEFFREY EPSTEIN and others" (EFTA00269912 — same Mar 9, 2011 interview as in EFTA01249058; shared with Story 2 and P46).

v3.4 (WS4) extension — victim-summary sheets: a run of eight redacted one-page victim-summary sheets from the Palm Beach investigation survives in DS9 (EFTA00216378 read in full as the exemplar; EFTA00216382, EFTA00216383, EFTA00216384, EFTA00216385, EFTA00216386, EFTA00216388, EFTA00216390 read in full as siblings). Each sheet records the girl's school at the time, the years, the number of sessions, and how she was brought to Epstein's house; the session counts in the run range from one to "over 100 times." No names are legible in the text layer and none is reproduced. The sheets are the investigation's victim-account record at summary level; per-sheet contents are the sheets' own record, not findings about any individual.

EFTA00013537 (Dec 11, 2007): de novo review of the evidence underlying the proposed indictment, prompted by Kirkland & Ellis correspondence; state interview audio/videotapes exist. EFTA00013774 (Feb 1, 2008): FBI/USA interviewed three girls; one broke down sobbing; a second was upset about the "18 month deal" in the paper and wanted jail time, not restitution; counseling arranged; four more girls coming in. EFTA00029921 (FD-1087, Jul 20, 2021 inventory): box 1B8, FBI Miami case 31E-MM-108062 — 7 VHS surveillance tapes PBPD 05-1205, 16 DVD-R discs, Cingular envelope/CD, microcassettes, T-160 cassette, green folder — collected Aug 28, 2006 from Palm Beach PD; 2005–06 surveillance media surviving into the 2021 federal inventory. EFTA00013785 (Jun 19, 2008): Stephanie D. Thacker (Allen Guthrie McHugh & Thomas, Charleston WV; former CEOS Principal Deputy Chief) to John Roth, DOJ — reacting to CEOS's May 15, 2008 letter re the federal Epstein investigation: argues the case "is best left to the state to resolve" and a federal prosecution "would appear to be selective"; "we continue to believe that after a complete, de novo, and independent review, the only appropriate conclusion will be that this case is best left to the state to resolve." Defense-side advocacy in the NPA window. (The May 15, 2008 CEOS letter itself is not in DS8; Thacker's enclosures are not identified.) EFTA00022654, Mar 30–Oct 10, 2005 entries (same file as P51): Mar 30, 2005 — surveillance and trash pulls begin; Detective investigating Epstein "as a suspect involved in a sexual battery of a 14 year old female"; Mar 31, 2005 — 17 trash bags collected, video surveillance Mar 31–Apr 3, 2005, six Maxell T-160 VHS tapes filed; Apr 1, 2005 — more trash/surveillance, a broken piece of a sexual toy (Cyclone Vibrator) photographed; Apr 5 and Apr 21, 2005 — further trash pulls; Jun 14, 2005 — airplane at Palm Beach International Airport, trash pulls requested; Sep 11–12, 2005 — marijuana-arrest interview (case 05-1263; prior intelligence that the arrestee "may have been paid money for sexual acts from Jeffrey Epstein" while under 18 — as stated in the file, not adopted as fact); Sep 21–Oct 10, 2005 — further trash pulls (case 05-368); Oct 11, 2005 note — "AS OF 10/11/2005 ALL NEW SUPPLEMENTS FOR JEFFREY EPSTEIN SHOULD BE FILED [under] 2600-8" (the file continues under a new number). Note: the underlying events overlap the DS9 PBPD case file (EFTA00227381, 2,265 pp.) already in Story 1; this document is the PBPD system-report narrative of them.

v3.39 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 2). EFTA00013589 (header dated Thu, 04 Dec 2008 22:24:05 +0000, as printed): an SDFL prosecutor circulates a draft letter to victims notifying them of Epstein's work release, with a blank still to be filled in, and asks for objections to the language. A draft; whether or when it was sent is not shown. EFTA00013733 (letter dated May 22, 2007; bulk-set item, read by keyword-window scan): Epstein's counsel writes to SDFL that he understands a decision on whether to seek an indictment would be made in the next month or two, and confirms that before any such decision defense attorneys will be given an opportunity to meet with the Office; the U.S. Attorney is copied. The defense's own confirmation, not the Office's reply.

v3.41 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 4). EFTA00013508 (emails dated Oct 16–22, 2007): in the NPA addendum negotiations, Epstein's counsel asks why the retired judge proposed as the independent third party should not simply represent the women, and objects to draft language on the selected lawyer's firm size, the statutory damages figure and discovery; the prosecutor replies that the idea is 'a non-starter', lists the Office's concessions, and asks for an answer on whether there is a deal by close of business Oct 23, 2007. Negotiating positions, not the executed text. EFTA00013503 (emails dated Oct 18, 2007): Epstein's counsel reports that the state attorney's office and court are available for Epstein to plead on November 20, and the U.S. Attorney's side agrees, subject to confirmation that this does not change when Epstein begins serving his sentence. EFTA00013528 (emails dated Nov 16–19, 2007): Epstein's counsel says the state court will take the plea and sentencing together on January 4, and the prosecutor notes that Epstein believes January 4 rather than December 14 is the date. A schedule in flux; the plea in fact took place later.

v3.42 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 5). EFTA00013606 (email dated Jul 3, 2007): the SDFL prosecutor reports defense requests for more time on several subpoenas and says she will agree to defer the financial-records subpoenas but wants the computer equipment removed from Epstein's home before the state search warrant 'as soon as possible', and will invite defense counsel to discuss a resolution of the federal investigation 'that could include concurrent time'. EFTA00013616 (emails dated Oct 15–16, 2007): a draft joint written submission to the independent third party describes the NPA's damages provision as covering 40 potential complainants on a list compiled by the United States, and the parties trade wording on whether either side may communicate with the third party or the selected attorney representative. Drafts, not the executed text. EFTA00013698 (letter from Epstein's counsel dated Nov 8, 2007): responding to the Office's Nov 5 letter, counsel says nothing in the NPA bars Epstein's agents from contacting potential witnesses but that they will cease such contact until the plea; that the state judge will not stagger plea and sentence, so both will occur by January 4, 2008; that Epstein must receive the same 18-month treatment as anyone else in Florida; and reserves objections to the § 2255 provisions. The defense's positions. EFTA00013706 (email dated Nov 27, 2007): the First Assistant tells Epstein's counsel that the defense has had a full week since being told of the independent third party's selection of the attorney representatives, cites the Justice for All Act notification duty, and says that unless a good-faith objection arrives by close of business Nov 28, 2007 he will authorize notifying the victims by letter after Nov 29. The attorney representatives are not named here. EFTA00013533 (defense letter dated Dec 7, 2007): Epstein's counsel transmits Epstein's signed Affirmation of the NPA and its October 30, 2007 Addendum, reports that the state plea and sentencing hearing is set for January 4, 2008 at 8:30 a.m., and asks the Office to hold off sending any victim notification letters until the contents can be discussed. EFTA00013550 (emails dated Mar 27–28, 2008): the SDFL prosecutor notes that the grand jury will not have a quorum on April 8, so if Epstein is not indicted on April 1 the next opportunity is April 15. Scheduling of a contingent indictment, not a decision to indict. EFTA00013730 (email dated Apr 25, 2008): the Office learns that one of Epstein's private investigators tracked down a victim who declined to speak with him and told her that her name might somehow appear in the press; she was referred to a pro bono lawyer and told of her right to contact the police. A report relayed to the prosecutor; the victim is not identified. EFTA00013918 (emails dated May 27–28, 2008): the SDFL prosecutor relays word, via the state attorney, that Epstein wants to serve less time (a figure of 90 days in jail is mentioned second-hand), says the original deal was supposed to be two years and that more victims have been identified since 18 months was agreed, and a supervisor says the U.S. Attorney and First Assistant have been clear that the Office is not negotiating further. Second-hand reports and internal views. EFTA00013834 (emails dated Mar 18–20, 2009, with a Mar 27, 2009 follow-up at EFTA00013605): after a meeting with one of Epstein's lawyers, the First Assistant writes that the Office will not interfere with how the Palm Beach Sheriff's Office administers Epstein's sentence, but does not condone mitigation and would object if asked about alternative custody or in-home detention, and expects no one to represent otherwise to the Sheriff; the lawyer later asks to put off any call to the Sheriff. EFTA00013855 (defense letter dated Jun 19, 2009): Epstein's counsel asks to discuss NPA paragraph 8, citing the U.S. Attorney's earlier acknowledgment that its language is 'far from simple', and argues that its waiver of liability covers at most a single § 2255 predicate per plaintiff and does not bar a statute-of-limitations defense. The defense's reading. EFTA00013858 (defense letter dated Sep 1, 2009): Epstein's counsel tells the Office that Epstein has finished the incarceration portion of his sentence, is serving community control at his Palm Beach home, and is applying under the interstate compact to transfer his supervision to the U.S. Virgin Islands, which has pre-approved the transfer on the same conditions; the letter is sent 'on the side of caution'. EFTA00013860 (emails dated Sep 17, 2009): as the Palm Beach Post counts down to the release of the agreement, an SDFL prosecutor suggests that, if anything is said, the Office's position (from earlier conversations with the U.S. Attorney) was that this began as a state case and he wanted it to remain one while setting minimum protections for victims in jail time and compensation, 'a floor, not a ceiling'; the writer adds a personal opinion about the state attorney that is labelled as such and not adopted here.

v3.43 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 6). EFTA00014100 (emails dated Jun 27–29, 2008): Epstein's state defense counsel confirms by email a Jun 27, 6:30 pm call in which the parties agreed the state plea agreement complied with the September 2007 NPA; the SDFL prosecutor, citing a state practitioner, asks that the word 'imprisoned' be inserted after 'six months' in the second sentencing paragraph, and on Jun 29 reports the change was accepted so the Monday plea 'looks like' it will go ahead; FBI notes that the Sheriff decides how the sentence is carried out (jail versus stockade). Correspondence before the plea, not the plea record. EFTA00013975 (email dated Jul 3, 2008; a duplicate copy is EFTA00014007): the SDFL prosecutor reports that a lawyer for three victims asked whether the Office could get out of the deal and was told that, assuming Epstein completes performance, the Office is bound; she also relays that, at a meeting with the Sheriff's Office, Epstein was said to be at the stockade, that his defense team had warned of suit over any less favorable treatment, and that he would be placed on work release, which she calls a contradiction of what the agents had been told earlier. Second-hand reports in an internal email. EFTA00014025 (email dated Aug 15, 2008): in a caseload certification exchange, the prosecutor says Operation Leap Year 'is still open, in case he breaches, but should be considered "on hold."' EFTA00014044 (emails dated Nov 20, 2008): the Office learns from the jail's Colonel that Epstein has been out on work release for 'the past few weeks'; the prosecutor writes that he spends days at his lawyer's office and adds that before the plea two defense lawyers had told her he would not get work release. Internal emails; the remark 'Can I indict him now?' is the writer's own. EFTA00014138 (email dated Nov 21, 2008): an internal reminder that 'the grand jury expires the end of Jan.' EFTA00014041 (emails dated Nov 25, 2008): an SDFL prosecutor and a law-enforcement colleague exchange notes on obtaining the work-release case file; one writes that if Epstein 'is going to run it will be in the next few days', and the other reports a drive-by of the house and asks to be told if the planes go anywhere. Expressed concern, not evidence of a flight attempt. EFTA00014030 (email dated Dec 15, 2008): the prosecutor reports that the Palm Beach police chief showed her a Palm Beach Daily News article and editorial, one of which makes clear the Office was not told of the work-release placement until well after the fact, and that the chief intended a public-records request for the Office's letter to the Sheriff's Office. EFTA00014175 (email dated Aug 4, 2009): the SDFL prosecutor reports hearing from several sources that Epstein is seeking state 'cooperation credit' to shorten home confinement for supposed help in the Madoff prosecution, which the Madoff AUSA had told her in no uncertain terms was not happening; flags a state docket entry, 'Agreed Order that the Order of Community Control is Corrected to Delete Special Condition #26 and #27', that the Office had not been told of; and asks whether new allegations may be investigated or referred, noting that the New York victims were never included in the identified-victim list. Rumors and questions, labelled as such in the source. EFTA00014178 (defense letter dated Dec 9, 2009; cover email EFTA00014177): Epstein's counsel confirms his place of employment is unchanged and says the spot where Palm Beach Police stopped him while walking was under 3 miles away on a direct route to work; reports that Epstein had filed a state civil RICO suit against the plaintiffs' firm at the centre of the Ponzi scheme exposed that autumn and one of its lawyers; alleges that the firm used the litigation and the NPA to deceive investors; complains that the Office's breach warnings stop Epstein from contesting claims; and asks the Office to consider ending contact with those lawyers. The defense's allegations, not findings.

v3.51 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 14). EFTA00019162 (emails dated Apr 14–20, 2011; continuations at EFTA00019163 and EFTA00019165): an FBI Miami Division agent in the West Palm Beach office asks the organizer of the New Orleans Investment Conference whether Epstein and a second person (redacted) attended between about 1998 and 2000, and which hotels it used then. The organizer lists the hotels for 1998–2000 but reports on Apr 20 that it could find no information on either person, saying its old databases had changed and its paper records were destroyed years earlier. The agent says the convention bureau will be the next call. This shows 2011 FBI investigative activity, which bears on Story 2's open 2010–2011 lead; it is recorded here, not as a Story 2 leg. The purpose of the inquiry is not stated.

v3.71 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 34). EFTA00013739 (undated draft non-prosecution agreement, text layer only): an earlier draft than the executed agreement. It recites three state solicitation counts and would have required Epstein to plead to three state offenses involving minors, with a joint, binding recommendation of 30 months (at least 20 months in prison without probation or community control in lieu of prison, then 10 months of community control), at least 17 months served after gain time, a victim list that 'will not exceed forty', a motion for a guardian ad litem for the identified victims, and plea and sentencing by September 28, 2007. It cites the Department's dual-prosecution policy as the federal interest. A draft; it is not the signed agreement, and the terms changed before signing. EFTA00013511 (draft letter dated October 2007 from the Office to a retired judge who had agreed to serve as special master): it explains the agreement's paragraphs 7A–7C and 8–10 on selecting and paying an attorney representative for the identified victims, quotes the civil-damages statute, and suggests selection criteria, including the ability to communicate with young women whose 'current ages are between 16 and 24' and experience against high-profile defense firms. A draft letter; whether this version was sent is not shown. EFTA00013623 (later version of the same special-master letter, undated in the text read): this version says the United States has 'identified 34 victims' under the statute, adds that the United States 'takes no position as to the validity of any such claim', and notes that defense counsel reserved the right to challenge litigation. A draft; the count is the letter's own figure at that stage. EFTA00013745 (letter dated October 9, 2007 from the U.S. Attorney to Epstein's counsel): he says the defense proposal on choosing victims' counsel falls outside the agreement and proposes instead that the Office ask the retired judge to help select one or more attorneys, working on contingency, with each victim free to use that attorney or choose her own, and with mediation by the same judge available if victims and their counsel want it. A proposal in correspondence. EFTA00013515 (emails dated Oct 16–22, 2007): the Office tells Epstein's counsel it intended the retired judge to select a lawyer for the victims, not to represent them himself, and that it does not want to choose the lawyer itself. The thread shows the defense obtaining wording changes to the draft letter to the special master, including a criterion about experience against high-profile attorneys 'who may test the veracity of the victims' claims'. Correspondence about a draft. EFTA00013506 (internal emails dated Oct 19, 2007): an SDFL prosecutor reports that a lawsuit filed in New York by one victim has made national news and suggests it may be the real reason the change of plea was delayed, because the defense is worried the guilty plea will be used in civil suits. She adds that several victims are getting calls from attorneys while the special master's choice is pending. The email also relays an unrelated third-party allegation, which is not carried here. Internal opinion and relayed reports. EFTA00013754 (internal email dated Nov 16, 2007): after an FBI meeting with the state prosecutor, the Office records that the plea and sentence were to happen on the same day to limit media attention, that the Sheriff's Office (not the state Department of Corrections) would decide work-release eligibility, and that the Office was checking whether anything barred work release for a sexual-predator designee. Epstein's counsel is recorded as confirming the defense would not contact other victims. Internal notes of conversations. EFTA00013549 (internal email dated Mar 19, 2008): the federal prosecutor reports that the first half of the grand jury presentation on the indictment was done the day before and that she overheard a grand juror say he had feared the case would be 'whitewash[ed]'. She says Epstein's lawyers were using the civil suits to subpoena victims for depositions, that a national crime-victims organization funded by a Justice Department grant had agreed to provide counsel, and she reports a serious welfare crisis involving one victim. The prosecutor's account in an internal email; no indictment was filed. EFTA00013656 (internal emails dated Mar 19–21, 2008, answering questions from a Justice Department reviewer): the federal prosecutor explains that the state indictment concerned two girls, only one of whom was in the draft federal indictment, and that 18 other girls named in the draft federal indictment were not part of the state case. She lists the agreement's three main terms (a registrable state plea, an 18-month term, and payment of damages) and describes Epstein's later efforts to avoid each one. She adds that the defense had demanded no contact with the State Attorney's Office, so she had not spoken to the state prosecutor in over six months, and she sets out the Florida speedy-trial and discharge risk if the state charges were dropped. The prosecutor's internal account. EFTA00013778 (internal email dated Mar 21, 2008): the prosecutor notes a three-year state limitations period on the prostitution charges, which she says had already run for several victims going back to 2001, and that the girls in the state indictment saw Epstein in February and September 2005. An internal legal note. EFTA00013659 — Victim/witness-related case material. The public atlas retains this source reference while omitting personal accounts, private identities and identifying circumstances. Any accounts, allegations or proposed testimony in the source are not treated as findings. Consult the entry’s other anchors for the procedural chain.
EFTA00013884 (internal emails dated May 27–28, 2008): told that the Deputy Attorney General was inclined to hear further defense arguments, the prosecutor drafts reasons against more delay. She cites the state limitations issue, victims growing older (which she says helps a mistake-of-age defense), a grand jury that would soon expire after 'more than a dozen hours of testimony' and that 'wants to indict', a promise of swift justice to the victims, and 'more than 20 known child victims'. The investigators add continued contact with victims by private investigators. Internal advocacy, not a finding. EFTA00013916 — Victim/witness-related case material. The public atlas retains this source reference while omitting personal accounts, private identities and identifying circumstances. Any accounts, allegations or proposed testimony in the source are not treated as findings. Consult the entry’s other anchors for the procedural chain.
EFTA00013878 (undated draft 'Notification of Identified Victims' prepared after the June 30, 2008 plea): it states that Epstein was sentenced to eighteen months followed by probation (the term is left partly blank) and gives notice that the listed individuals are people the Office was prepared to name as victims in an indictment. The list runs Jane Doe #1 and Jane Doe #3 through Jane Doe #30 under the draft's own pseudonyms (Jane Doe #2 is not listed), with an acknowledgment for Epstein to sign through his attorney. A draft; the figures differ from the later notices. EFTA00014087 (internal email dated Jun 30, 2008, replying to a forwarded wire story on the plea): the prosecutor says the detail missing from press reports is that Epstein must pay damages of 'a minimum of $150,000 to each of 31 girls'. Her own characterization in an internal email; the count differs from other drafts. EFTA00013923 (internal email dated Aug 5, 2008): the prosecutor reviews whether the Office has a written, binding agreement that includes the December 2007 modification. She notes that before the plea the Office had told the defense it already had a binding agreement; that a few hours after the June 30, 2008 plea she and the agents gave defense counsel the proposed victim notification; and that defense counsel's July 9 letter, which asked for a shorter one-page notice, could be read as written assent to the quoted condition. She voices concern about appearing to change position. Internal legal analysis. EFTA00013949 (letter dated Aug 20, 2008 from the Office to Epstein's counsel): the Office says the special master's chosen attorney representative will continue and needs written confirmation that his fees will be paid. It offers to 'revert to the shorter list' of victims prepared when the agreement was signed in September 2007 'so long as the United States may proceed to prosecute your client for those victims identified after that date', or else treat all victims known as of June 30, 2008 as entitled to compensation. It asks for an election and says it must correct incorrect information previously given to victims. The Office's position in correspondence; the defense election is not in this document. EFTA00013947 — Victim/witness-related case material. The public atlas retains this source reference while omitting personal accounts, private identities and identifying circumstances. Any accounts, allegations or proposed testimony in the source are not treated as findings. Consult the entry’s other anchors for the procedural chain.
EFTA00013955 (letter dated Sep 16, 2008 from a plaintiffs' firm to the federal prosecutor): the firm objects to the Office's September 2, 2008 letters to victims, saying they steer victims to a particular attorney who would make unsolicited contact, understate what the damages waiver gives up, and overstate the value of Epstein's agreement to pay fees. It demands that the Office stop and send corrective letters, and that its clients be contacted only through the firm. The firm's position, not a finding. EFTA00013801 (undated defense rebuttal to the First Assistant's May 19, 2008 letter): Epstein's counsel claim that the CEOS review was neither independent nor de novo; that at a September 7, 2007 meeting the Office set a September 21 deadline or the defense would face 'an already-drafted 53-page indictment, purportedly identifying 40 minors, with a guideline range of 188 months'; that a federal official had insisted on two years of state imprisonment; and that the Office's earlier proposed victims' attorney presented an undisclosed conflict. Defense claims and characterizations, not findings. EFTA00013811 (undated defense submission to the Office of the Deputy Attorney General, mid-2008): Epstein's counsel ask the Office to end federal involvement and return the case to the State. They argue that none of the three federal statutes fits without a novel reading, citing two June 2008 Supreme Court decisions on narrow construction; that state limitations periods bar most conduct; that Epstein spent at least 100 days a year in Palm Beach, so travel there was going home; and they quote deposition excerpts from women who said they had lied about their ages. Defense advocacy; the quoted witnesses are not identified here.

v3.73 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 36). EFTA00016016 (undated victim-by-victim charts from the draft Florida federal indictment, partly OCR text, lower confidence; companions EFTA00016004, EFTA00016005, EFTA00016006, EFTA00016010, EFTA00016011 and EFTA00016013): each page lists, for one Jane Doe [minor at the time, per the document], the numbered overt acts and counts naming Epstein: conspiracy-to-entice overt acts, enticement of a minor to engage in prostitution, travel to engage in illicit sexual conduct, and recruiting or obtaining a minor for commercial sex. The dates printed run from March 2004 to October 2005; overt-act numbers reach at least 156 and count numbers at least 60. Draft charging charts, never filed; charges are allegations, and the OCR-read pages are lower confidence.

v3.75 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 38). EFTA00020532 (FBI electronic communication dated 12/06/2006, partly OCR text, lower confidence): the Palm Beach resident agency, which began investigating Epstein on 07/24/2006 after receiving the Palm Beach police files, sets leads for other FBI offices. It says computer processing units were removed from the house before the police search and never recovered, that message pads recovered in the search show messages from girls who had been interviewed, and that prosecutors and agents had a target date of January 2007 for indictment, citing media coverage, the victims' vulnerability and political influences. The FBI's account as written; not findings. EFTA00020797 (Palm Beach police incident report, 2006, dates partly blank): a detective records calls from people involved in the case saying they were being followed by a driver who drove aggressively and ran one of them off the road, and records an analysis of subpoenaed phone records showing calls on one day between Epstein's phone, an assistant and a victim. A police report with names and numbers redacted; allegations, not findings. EFTA00021249 (USAO Southern District of Florida letter dated July 10, 2008): a notice letter to counsel stating that the individuals identified are those the United States was prepared to name as victims of an enumerated offense, referring to Epstein's state plea and sentence of twelve months followed by community control. The letter as printed; the list itself is not reproduced.

v3.76 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 39). EFTA00023506 (FBI collected-items report run 08/10/2007, case 31E-MM-108062; companion EFTA00023516, chain-of-custody forms from September 2006): items received from the Palm Beach police on 08/28/2006 include phone message books and pads, shredded paper, massage tables, framed and unframed photographs, CDs and video tapes, a computer processing unit from the office, flash cards, a high school transcript, recorded calls, photo line-ups, surveillance tapes and trash-pull papers, with later additions in 2007 such as a massage book. An evidence inventory; item contents are not described and nothing here is a finding.

v3.77 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 40). EFTA00024806 (Palm Beach police report narrative 13, dated 10/20/05): the officer leading the crime scene team records that on October 20, 2005 the team stood by at about 8:30 a.m., arrived at the residence at about 9:33 a.m., inventoried, photographed and videotaped the search, including a walk-through at entry and exit, finished at about 3:05 p.m., and told a man who said he was the defendant's lawyer that the house was secured and the inventory return left inside. A police narrative; officers are not named.

v3.80 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 43). EFTA00030866 (federal grand-jury subpoena issued Mar 2, 2007 in the Southern District of Florida, FGJ 07-103): the recipient (redacted) is commanded to appear in West Palm Beach on March 13, 2007 with all documents relating to Epstein, including billing statements, payment records, appointment books, treatment notes and correspondence. A subpoena form; the return of service is blank in this copy.

stories.entry_markdown:
Span: 2009–2019.
Anchors: EFTA00230786 (Jun 12, 2009 SDFL "willfully violated
Term 8" letter, 1,131 pp).
Endpoint: the Jun 12, 2009 breach declaration (document-verified).
Dated stopping point: Jun 12, 2009 (EFTA00230786) is the endpoint; the documented record runs to Sep 26, 2011 (EFTA00205768) — the 2010–2011 investigation is now its own story, P46.
DOWNGRADED in v3.0 (WS4): confirmed → probable. Two v2.1 anchors do
not support the story and were removed — EFTA00039665 (May 21, 2021
email forwarding a Knight Capital / SEC whistleblower appeal; nothing
about the NPA, breach, or federal inaction) and EFTA00039367 (Sep 17,
2019 BOP psychological-reconstruction memo; post-death, nothing about
the 2009 breach or the 2009–2019 period). The "no federal prosecution
until the July 2019 case" half has no supporting anchor at all and is
bounded here as an unanchored claim, not a verified finding — it rests
on the slice + prior findings, not a search of all federal dockets.
v3.1 narrows the title/endpoint to the breach declaration alone. A
confirmed tier for that narrowed story would be defensible on its two
anchors, but the tier is kept probable pending review — the v3.0
downgrade was the correction, and re-tiering it is a review decision,
not taken unilaterally in a fix pass.

Open lead (partly answered in v3.3 — see P46): whether no federal prosecution followed the breach declaration until the July 2019 case, and why — the "decade of inaction" question. For 2010–2011 it is now answered in part: a new criminal investigation with victim interviews was opened (Jul–Oct 2010) and a preliminary investigation ran to Mar 2011, then the USAO declined to move forward (P46). Whether anything followed between late 2011 and the 2018–2019 case is still not established in the material read, and the question is kept open for that period.
Links: 1, 3.
v2.0 DS8 extension: EFTA00013587 documents the victim-notification
mechanics whose failure OPR later called poor judgment (see new
Story 25, the OPR investigation — the accountability counterpart).

v3.2 (WS5) extension — NPA-negotiation paper (NONPROSECUTION sample): EFTA00067260 (DS8): "CONFIDENTIAL PLEA NEGOTIATIONS — TERMS OF EPSTEIN NON-PROSECUTION AGREEMENT": Epstein pleads guilty (not nolo contendere) to an Information filed by the Palm Beach County State Attorney charging lewd and lascivious battery on a child, in violation of Fl. Stat. — a 1-page negotiation terms sheet. EFTA00013521 (DS8, Oct 31, 2007): AUSA email to Jay Lefkowitz re NPA paragraph 8 ("we are beginning to think about what discovery we may need to take to verify any claims"). EFTA00013968 (DS8, Jun 19, 2008): AUSA email re speaking with Roy Black about resolving the federal and state litigation. EFTA00014110 (DS8, Nov 24, 2008): USAO letter to Roy Black re Epstein. Post-NPA correspondence. EFTA00214042 / EFTA00214043 (DS9, Aug 18, 2009): AUSA email chain responding to a book/documentary author's inquiry: "There are no documents that were filed in connection with this case except some sealed matters. We deferred prosecution in favor of the state's prosecution of Epstein." A contemporaneous (Aug 2009) AUSA statement of the deferral posture.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — breach pre-history + 2010–2011 aftermath (the endpoint, the Jun 12, 2009 declaration, is unchanged): Jun 9, 2009 — "Operation Leap Year: Notification of Breach" memo (Sloman, Acting USA) (EFTA00189787, 14 pp.): seeks approval to serve the breach notice at the Jun 12, 2009 Marra hearing; recommends "proceed to indictment promptly thereafter" (no federal indictment followed in 2009 — the recommendation's outcome is not established in the memo); case-by-case survey of 13 civil suits and the breach theory (the most conservative reading of the NPA requires Epstein to waive challenges to liability where the plaintiff proceeds exclusively under 18 U.S.C. § 2255). Nov 26, 2008 — USAO letter: "Mr. Epstein has not breached the Non-Prosecution Agreement… by serving a portion of his 18-month sentence of imprisonment in the Palm Beach County Work Release Program" (EFTA00178359) — the pre-breach position the Second Addendum later superseded. The "SECOND ADDENDUM TO NON-PROSECUTION AGREEMENT" (EFTA00216077): recitals (NPA Sep 24, 2007; Addendum Oct 29, 2007; USAO gave notice it considers current work-release participation a material breach; Epstein disputes breach); new ¶2(a): consecutive 12 + 6 months county jail, no withholding/probation/community control; confined 24 h/day to the Stockade except work release from Mar 24, 2009 under PBSO rules (≤48 hours/week outside, GPS + deputy escort, work log weekly to USAO); breach of any condition allows the US to terminate the Agreement and prosecute Epstein "and any other individual or entity for any and all federal offenses." Signature blocks present; the Dated: lines are blank in the text layer — date of execution NOT established from this copy. Sep 26, 2011 — internal USAO thread re CVRA relief: "Setting aside the non-pros and prosecuting him as though the Non-pros had never been signed"; the Jane Does' desired relief was to set aside the NPA; a USAO voice argued Epstein "already served his sentence in state court and performed all his other obligations under the Non-Pros (including paying damages to 30-some girls)" and it would be a Due Process violation to suggest setting it aside (EFTA00205768 — shared with P1). The 2010–2011 investigation legs (shared with new story P46, where the episode is told whole): Oct 21, 2010 — Cassell to USAO: in late Jul 2010, Mike Fisten and others met the FBI re Epstein's sexual abuse of "other young girls — girls not covered by the non-prosecution agreement"; USAO reply: "Interviews have been conducted of potential new victims. Let me check in with the case agent and get back to you" (EFTA00206650). Mar 9, 2011 — AUSA memo "Highly Confidential — Preliminary Investigation of Additional Crimes of Jeffrey Epstein and Others" (EFTA01249058, 3 pp.): a victim reported being flown around the US and Europe to have sex with prominent men, encounters videotaped, paid after each encounter; the memo lists named men as reported by the victim via Edwards/Fisten; Clinton came to Epstein's house several times and received erotic massages (not from her), at least once while still president; obstruction allegations (perjury, falsified probation records, a lawyer threatening a subpoenaed victim); a modeling agency as a front for trafficking with fraudulent visa applications. All of this is the victim's reported account as relayed by Edwards/Fisten to the AUSA in a preliminary-investigation memo; the AUSA states a formal memo with analysis is to follow. No finding is recorded in it. Cite only with that framing. Mar 24, 2011 — Daily Beast email to Roy Black: the Daily Beast received a letter from former US Attorney Alex Acosta describing the NPA negotiations; per the Daily Beast's summary, Acosta's letter says Epstein's defense team (a) negotiated in bad faith, agreeing to terms then appealing to DOJ in Washington; (b) investigated prosecutors' personal lives/families to discredit/disqualify two prosecutors — attempt failed; (c) threatened Acosta that his "excessive zeal" could become a book (EFTA00664159 — cite as the Daily Beast's summary of Acosta's letter, not as the letter itself). May 18, 2010 — Palm Beach Post: Podhurst Orseck sued Epstein claiming he refused to pay its $2 million legal bill for representing more than a dozen young women; Epstein had agreed to pay for an attorney for 33 women; the firm's claim is that failure to pay "constitutes 'a material breach'" of the NPA (the firm's allegation in its suit, labeled as such) (EFTA00190244).

v3.4 (WS4) extension — breach pre-history, Jun 2, 2009: USAO internal email (EFTA00212882, DS9, 1 p.; EFTA00014173 is the Jun 3, 2009 reply copy): Judge Marra asked the USAO to appear Fri, Jun 12 to address whether Epstein's defense of the civil suits breaches the NPA; the Palm Beach Post moved to intervene to unseal the NPA (hearing set Wed, Jun 10); Epstein's May 26, 2009 pleading arguing §2255 claims must all be dismissed because he was never convicted of a federal offense "directly contradicts the Non-Prosecution Agreement"; "At this point, I believe that Epstein is probably in breach of the Agreement… We are required to provide him with 'timely notice' of his breach and file an indictment within 60 days of learning of the breach. That means that we need to indict by July 24th." The immediate pre-history of the Jun 9, 2009 breach memo (EFTA00189787) and the Jun 12 declaration; no federal indictment followed in 2009 (see the v3.3 extension).

extensions_v38.text: 5 documents, pre-history and mid-span legs; mapped 2019 case scope and endpoint unchanged. EFTA00009975 and EFTA00009976 record an SDNY exchange on Nov 30, 2018 asking whether the matter is open, answered "Yes. As of today", followed by a staffing discussion. This is prosecutor-level opening correspondence, not a replacement for the separately carried FBI formal initiation date of Dec 6, 2018. EFTA00009977 records planning a Nov 30 call on the way forward and, on Dec 4, a Thursday meeting with case agents to discuss next steps. Scheduling is not proof of the meeting's content or occurrence. EFTA00009936 (May 15, 2019) transmits an attachment named as the May 10 ODAG status memo, requesting close handling because the investigation was covert. Memo contents are not supplied. EFTA00014467 (Jun 27, 2019) says prosecutors obtained the NPA side-letter list and their principal New York victim was not listed; the writer says the listed people appear to be in Florida. No identities are reproduced, and this assessment is not a judicial ruling on NPA scope.

extensions_v311.text: Pre-arrest list cross-check, not a blanket NPA-scope ruling. EFTA00014466 (1 p., Jun 27, 2019) is an SDNY Public Corruption Unit email saying the office obtained the NPA side-letter's victim list and checked that its then-principal complainant was not on it; the writer says the listed victims appear to be Florida victims. This is the prosecutor's contemporaneous comparison and qualified geographic assessment, not an independently repeated identity reconciliation, an exhaustive finding about every complainant, or a judicial determination of the NPA's enforceability in New York. No victim identity is given. It adds a documented pre-arrest rationale without collapsing the CVRA and SDNY proceedings, changing an endpoint or tier, or implying wrongdoing from association.

The investigation itself remains an open end (OIG draft report
Mar 2023, EFTA00035986; guards' prosecution is Story 24). Note: the Aug 19

v3.2 (WS2) MAJOR extension — the OIG final report and BOP's status update (also a Story 24 leg): EFTA00035907 (6 pp.): BOP Program Review Division memorandum, July 15, 2024, "Status Update to the Office of Inspector General's (OIG) Final Report dated June 26, 2023: Investigation and Review of the Federal Bureau of Prisons' Custody, Care, and Supervision of Jeffrey Epstein at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York, New York." Supporting minor legs (Story 4): BOP Office of General Counsel legal-hold notice for the inmate death, August 14, 2019 (EFTA00036429, 3 pp.); SHU staffing talking points, August 13, 2019 — "all posts in SHU were filled 8/9 and 8/10 correct? … trying to combat sound bite that staffing shortages led to suicide" (EFTA00036567, 1 p.) — the staffing-shortage framing is contested inside the record itself; the After Action Review Team arrival memo, August 14, 2019 (EFTA00036620); MCC draft press release, August 10, 2019 (EFTA00035418 — asks whether next of kin was notified and whether staff initiated life-saving measures); two MCC subpoenas (August 20 and August 21, 2019, the latter re "Outlaw calls") forwarded January 31, 2020 (EFTA00029801); DHO hearing packets for the July 23, 2019 incident, delivered August 1, 2019 (EFTA00034784); psych-observation windows July 8, 6 p.m.–July 10, 9 a.m. (EFTA00035062) and July 24 (EFTA00034929); clinical encounter July 28, 2019 (neuropathy follow-up) (EFTA00033804, 21 pp.); MCC photo sheet for the August 10, 2019 suicide incident, photographs taken 6:49 a.m. (EFTA00024376, 20 pp.); suicide-watch/psych-observation log, observation started July 21, 2019 (EFTA00035225, 28 pp.).

Note: Story 4 already has a Dec 2019 "preserved" → Jan 9, 2020 "wrong tier… no longer exists" hallway-video item — the Aug 8 "broken" camera report is an earlier, distinct item. Post-death mortality-review scheduling (30-day deadline). EFTA00075817 / EFTA00087826 / EFTA00128629 (DS9, Aug 11–14, 2019): internal comms thread: "Jonathan Dienst keeps trying to confirm if Epstien was on suicide watch... remember to stick to the script. *Can't comment on that." Post-death press handling of the suicide-watch question (three copies/variants of one thread). EFTA00140423 (DS9, 47 pp): Form 583 Report of Incident, Jul 23, 2019, 1:27 AM, SHU (Main Facility, Housing Unit, Special Housing Unit; FBI Notified: No; USMS Notified: No). The incident report itself — distinct from the already-anchored Jul 25, 2019 email relay of the BOP report (EFTA00014628). v3.3 (WS1) extension — reconstruction text + 2021 OIG statement (the OIG final report, Jun 26, 2023, remains the later endpoint via the WS2 leg above): Sep 2019 — BOP "PSYCHOLOGICAL RECONSTRUCTION OF INMATE DEATH" (Epstein, register 76318-054, died Aug 10, 2019) (EFTA00105651, 12 pp.), prepared by the National Suicide Prevention Coordinator team per BOP Program Statement 5324.08. Stated limitations: "Formal interviews were not conducted as a part of this reconstruction at the direction of the Department of Justice"; "there was no such video in this case since the original video was confiscated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) prior to the beginning of this reconstruction. The absence of these two areas of inquiry severely limited the ability to establish accurate timelines, confirm subjective reports, establish converging and diverging lines of facts, or discover new areas of inquiry." (Distinct from the already-anchored Sep 17, 2019 transmittal memo EFTA00123213 — that is the memo; this is the reconstruction itself.) Sep 22, 2021 — OIG digitally recorded sworn statement of Mark Epstein (OIG case 2019-010614), NY Field Office (EFTA00113482, 94 pp.): Mark Epstein (Jeffrey's brother) reached out to OIG; he initially assumed suicide, then concluded from the autopsy that "there's no way in the world you would say it was a suicide"; the city pathologist "could not call this a suicide… too many questionable things, you know, like the broken bones in his neck"; Dr. [Baden] confirmed "not to call this a suicide. It looks much more like a homicide." Cite as Mark Epstein's statements to OIG, not as a finding — the OIG's own report (Jun 2023) concluded suicide; the statement is the brother's position as recorded.

v3.4 (WS4) extension — institutional-response closure, May 14, 2020: BOP Reentry Services Division memorandum (Assistant Director → Regional Director, Northeast Region) (EFTA00121398, DS9, 22 pp.; EFTA00139235 is the duplicate copy): "I have reviewed your Institution Response, dated January 27, 2020, to the Psychological Reconstruction of an inmate suicide at MCC New York. The corrective actions and plans for implementation in your response are appropriate." The memo carries the reconstruction text as an attachment (the same attachment text as EFTA00105651). v3.5 (WS1) extension — DS8 metadata-only survey. 21 legs; the OIG final-report thread is extended to Jun 30, 2025 via BOP status updates. EFTA00013176 (Aug 10, 2019): possible hoax call from someone claiming to be an MCC investigator telling an Epstein associate the body was ready for pickup; SDNY asks BOP to confirm; defense counsel concerned about hoax information; morning information flow — 7:52 a.m. ambulance → 8:18 a.m. "passed" → press release before counsel notified. The people and underlying conduct are not identified in the text; this is a limited statement of charging intent, not an exoneration, a blanket closure, or an account of the interviews. EFTA00016910 (2 pp.; July 25, 2019 MDT, America/Denver) records an MCC instruction to preserve the SHU-tier footage around the July incident, supply an investigation copy and maintain a court/counsel copy, followed by a Special Investigative Technician's reply, 'Done.' EFTA00016417 (3 pp.; December 17, 2019 MST, America/Denver) carries counsel's earlier July 25 preservation request and an MCC reply saying appropriate staff had been asked to preserve the footage and MCC staff did not have body cameras. In the December message, counsel complains that the video was not retained despite the preservation request and confirmation. These documents verify the request, preservation/completion representations and later counsel complaint, not an independent inventory of what footage was actually copied, retained, lost or destroyed or the cause of non-retention. This concerns the July incident, not August 10 death footage. Separately, EFTA00016903 (1 p.) is an OIG memorandum concerning an August 14, 2019 interview about the night of August 9 and morning of August 10: the agent reports a verbal voluntary-interview explanation, mistakenly supplying a required-information warning form that the MCC lieutenant read and signed, and identifies the voluntary-warning form intended. The memo says those present believed the interviewee understood the answers were voluntary and not compelled. This is an investigators' procedural account, not a judicial ruling on voluntariness or admissibility, interview testimony establishing cause of death, or a guilt finding. The death endpoint, Reyes non-merge, prior cell-use limits and EFTA00015515 date-inconsistency flag remain unchanged.

v3.14 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). Three FBI technical-update documents add a bounded DVR-extraction and repair sequence, not an independent forensic audit. EFTA00017950 (2 pp.; forwarded March 9, 2020 MDT, America/Denver, containing August 14, 2019 updates) attributes to MCC staff a July 29 failure of two or three drives in DVR system 2 and reports that two of the three camera feeds of interest were on that system and were not recording on August 10. It reports suspension of the systems' overwrite cycles on August 12 and August 10 respectively, warns of possible corruption/encryption and explicitly allows that reconstruction could fail. A plan to export the July interval is not proof that it was recovered. EFTA00017949 (1 p.; same March forwarding date, embedded August 14 update) reports that priority cameras from DVR 1 had completed downloading; replacement-system activation, staging/transcoding and collection are still prospective in that message. These are attributed technical status accounts concerning the later extraction effort, distinct from the July-incident preservation instruction/assurance and counsel complaint carried in v3.13. Existing endpoints, the Reyes non-merge and the EFTA00015515 date inconsistency remain unchanged.

v3.15 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00019067 (2 pp.; August 11, 2019 MDT, America/Denver) records counsel transmitting the family's broad preservation and production request covering detention records, the July incident and the August 10 death, including relevant video, communications and physical evidence. The scope of a request is not an inventory of existing or preserved material, and its references to both events do not make their footage interchangeable. EFTA00019069 (1 p.; August 12, 2019 MDT) asks that the request be forwarded and seeks DNA collection from cell ligatures/bedding, while separately requesting privilege screening for seized emails. These are requests, not proof of forwarding, testing, taint-review implementation or production. EFTA00019233 (2 pp.; January 8–17, 2020 MST) records BOP proposing a Board of Inquiry into MCC operations, including special housing, cameras, training and staffing; OIG seeks FBI/SDNY positions and participants arrange further discussion. BOP describes this as an operational review, not a misconduct investigation, and promises to avoid conflict with the criminal case and refer new misconduct allegations. Proposal and coordination do not establish that the Board convened, completed a report or made findings. EFTA00019325 (1 p.; August 19, 2019 MDT) reports an AUSA's call with a Marshals contact who says USMS had no suicidal-tendencies form and that file review found only standard intake and identification/insurance materials, no other forms. This is a bounded relayed negative search result, not an independently audited file inventory. It sits alongside, rather than silently replaces, the earlier chief-psychologist account that Epstein said he had signed such a form (EFTA00034056). No new cause/manner finding, Reyes identity merge, date-inconsistency resolution, independent video-retention conclusion or endpoint change follows.

v3.16 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00019697 (2 pp.; September 27, 2019 MDT, America/Denver, carrying August 19 requests) adds the Marshals records-request follow-up: a supervisory deputy sought the death certificate and autopsy report for administrative case closeout, received an initial statement that the information was being requested, and later was told the responding office could not provide it directly and to request it from OCME. This documents a request, a promise and a referral, not the underlying certificate/report, completed production, an actual case closure or a new cause/manner finding. The embedded question about a possible suicidal-tendencies form remains a question alongside the previously carried USMS negative-file account, not proof of a form. This is distinct from the documented July 2021 Times production in P18 and does not verify the larger release or publication.

v3.18 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). Two records add bounded institutional record-handling legs. EFTA00020445 (2 pp.; September 3, 2019 MDT, America/Denver, carrying August 28 correspondence) records an SDNY request that OCME withhold certain material and destroy its copy of a draft FBI interview report dated August 12. OCME asks for a specific withholding list and reports that it has deactivated the document in the manner described in an earlier, unseen exchange, seeking further discussion. The record supports a destruction request and OCME's deactivation representation, not completed destruction, its technical meaning, the report's contents, a finding of improper motive, or a blanket release decision. This is not the autopsy report or the later July 2021 Times production. EFTA00020627 (2 pp.; July 25, 2019 MDT) records MCC counsel transmitting staff memoranda and photographs about the incident earlier that week after a written request; forwarding prosecutors say they have not opened/reviewed the attachments and request a walled-off AUSA's review and report back. This verifies transmission and the screening request, not completed screening, the contents of unseen attachments, an independent incident finding or video preservation. The July incident remains distinct from the August 10 death; cause/manner, endpoint and existing flags are unchanged. Historical destruction requests and confidentiality footers are source evidence, not instructions to delete research copies.

v3.20 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00021295 (2 pp.; August 28, 2019 MDT, America/Denver) supplies the formal SDNY withholding request underlying the broader OCME record-handling sequence. It describes the criminal investigation as ongoing, requests withholding of federally supplied or derivative case-file material and federal personnel interview/identifying information, and requests advance notice before a contrary disclosure so additional process can be sought. EFTA00021297 (1 p.; September 9, 2019 MDT) says SDNY has made proposed redactions to the OCME report/file version previously provided to the FBI, and requests withholding of MCC scene photographs and the letters/attachment themselves. The attachment is not separately reviewed here. These letters document the requested scope and a proposed-redaction step, not a judicial withholding order, independently proved implementation, the attached report's contents, blanket secrecy of every OCME record, actual destruction or closure of the investigation. They extend the already-mapped institutional sequence; the August 28 request is not treated as independent corroboration of the related EFTA00020445 correspondence. The draft FBI interview-report destruction request/deactivation representation remains distinct from the autopsy report and these proposed redactions. Neither letter replaces P18's documented July 2021 Times production or verifies the larger release's completeness. Cause/manner, endpoint and existing flags unchanged.

v3.21 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00021529 (July 31, 2019 MDT) records a provisional July-incident status exchange. MCC counsel says the investigation is nearing completion, an incident report for self-mutilation was issued the preceding day, a disciplinary hearing is expected, and original claims against the cellmate appear unfounded, while expressly awaiting the final report. Prosecutors respond that until a final report is received they plan to tell the court the investigation is ongoing. These are attributed interim accounts and a planned court position, not a final investigative or disciplinary finding, proof of what caused the injuries, a held hearing, receipt of the final report or closure. The July incident remains distinct from the August 10 death and does not resolve the disputed accounts already mapped.

v3.22 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00022022 (June 30, 2021 MDT) records prosecutors comparing an earlier interview account with a reported later OIG denial concerning knowledge that Epstein was without a cellmate. One sender attributes to earlier notes an account of knowing, not notifying others and awaiting a replacement, contrasts it with the later reported denial, and asks about recollection/accuracy; a colleague says the earlier account matches their memory and was included in the prosecution memorandum. These are attributed interview-note/recollection accounts, not independent review of the underlying interviews or memorandum, a finding that either account is true, actual knowledge, a false-statement ruling, or resolution of the cellmate issue. No redacted identity is inferred or merged with Reyes; this does not resolve the already-flagged July 30, 2020 inconsistency or conflate the earlier July injury incident with August 10.

v3.23 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00022636 (August 12–14, 2019 MDT, America/Denver) records internal SDNY document-preservation instructions followed by a formal litigation-hold notice in connection with the death and a potential family wrongful-death case: preserve records about Epstein beyond the death/earlier injury incident, avoid altering existing versions, return EOUSA forms identifying records/locations, and suspend routine email deletions for recipients. One respondent transmits a form described as completed and represents a received-email archive practice, sent-mail location, and no substantive texts. The unseen form, backup adequacy and actual system-wide hold implementation are not independently verified; instructions and one custodian's account are not a completeness audit or proof that all material survived. These email/document holds are distinct from the separately bounded July-video preservation accounts and do not conflate the July incident with August 10. EFTA00023013 (September 3–8, 2020 MDT) records requests for an official/final suicide-reconstruction report for AUSAs and an attributed response that the request was forwarded up the leadership chain and was being processed without a specific timeframe. Other correspondents say they do not hold or have not seen the report. This documents routing/status representations, not production, verified report existence or contents, institutional absence, destruction, completed review, or a new cause/manner or closure finding.

EFTA00018023 and EFTA00031980 (Jul 29 to 30, 2021) record CBP's warning that outbound travel between 1990 and 2000 was not recorded as it is today, and that the TECS records already supplied were all it could provide for Maxwell and Epstein for that period. The statement about two surname variants elsewhere in the chain concerns a redacted person, who is not identified here. extensions_v39.text: Three connected discovery-scope records, not an additional story. EFTA00013243 (1 p., Oct 9 to 10, 2020) records supervisors agreeing not to recollect an original Florida agent's emails with an AUSA because the OPR-collected material was expected to encompass them, while separately seeking agent correspondence with witnesses and other potentially discoverable documents. Completeness is the prosecutors' expectation, not an independently demonstrated fact. EFTA00013202 (3 pp., Oct 30, 2020; overlapping thread also opened as EFTA00013205) records that PAE had deduplicated roughly 40,000 images without being asked, requiring the production to be redone. It expressly distinguishes those images, FBI Florida boxes and FOIA-office records from electronic-device productions, which the writer said had not yet been sent to the team. Rolling delivery and timing estimates do not establish complete delivery by Nov 9. EFTA00011251 (2 pp., Dec 4 to 8, 2020) says the responsiveness review was complete and requests locking off 397,365 documents not tagged responsive, leaving 1,218,719 tagged responsive accessible; the later message describes limiting future device review to identified responsive material. These are workspace/tagging counts in the correspondence, not a count of unique DS8 PDFs, a corpus census, or proof the access restriction was implemented. No inference about unreviewed contents or undisclosed wrongdoing follows. Endpoint unchanged.

extensions_v312.text: Three newly read records add bounded discovery and subpoena steps. EFTA00016032 (2 pp., December 18, 2020) is the Government's replacement-production letter: it says an inadvertent Bates-stamping error caused overlaps and that Deutsche Bank and UBS materials were reproduced under corrected numbers SDNY_GM_02742184–02742302. The letter documents the production representation and index, not independent verification of every underlying record or all discovery gaps. EFTA00015636 (5 pp., March 29–April 23, 2021) preserves defense requests and the Government's response: requested email attachments were not recovered from searched devices, and no additional original metadata was recovered for carved/deleted files; the writer is not aware of additional metadata in the Government's possession. For vendor-converted recordings, the Government says September–October 2020 timestamps reflect conversion, not original recording dates. These are the Government's bounded recovery/production explanations, not a finding that attachments never existed, that records were destroyed, that all metadata was independently audited, or that every discovery dispute was resolved. EFTA00015859 (6 pp., filed June 4, 2021, docket 298) is Judge Nathan's order denying the requested Rule 17(c)(3) subpoena: the court rejects the broader journal/original-photograph requests on relevance/impeachment grounds and treats requests for items the Government represented would be available for inspection as moot. This verifies that procedural ruling, not the truth of the underlying allegations or completion of the promised inspections. Private journal contents, photographs and identifying descriptions are not reproduced.

extensions_v314.text: EFTA00017848 (1 p.; August 25, 2021, docket 329) is an actual order concerning attorney-client video-teleconference disruptions: Judge Nathan finds MDC Legal's assurance that communications had not been interfered with, recorded or listened to sufficient, expresses confidence in trial preparation, and directs prompt notice of further problems after good-faith conferral with the Government and MDC Legal. The order records the court's assessment of the assurances, not an independent technical audit or a guarantee against future disruption. EFTA00017847 (1 p.; September 2, 2021 MDT, America/Denver) is counsel's subsequent notification alleging suspicious activity during the prior day's Webex session, saying an MDC staff member witnessed it and requesting an explanation/remediation before reporting to the court. This verifies a renewed complaint, not that interference or surveillance was independently proved, that remediation occurred, or that the court later adopted the allegation. Order and later allegation remain distinct. No victim identities or identifying descriptions are reproduced, and no tier or endpoint is changed.

EFTA00026750 (Government letter filed July 28, 2020, Dkt. 33): on the protective order, the Government opposes Maxwell's request to be free to name publicly anyone who has spoken about Epstein or Maxwell to the media, in public fora or in litigation, offering instead that the defense may name victims who identify themselves on the record in this case, use names in sealed filings and in private investigation; it also opposes limits on the Government's use of its own materials, citing FOIA and Touhy obligations and noting that such requests have been received. Positions in a filing; the Court's ruling is not in this document. EFTA00026519 (SDNY and FBI emails dated Jul 1–2, 2020): on the eve of Maxwell's arrest, the FBI sends victim-notification staff a spreadsheet, dated June 26, 2020, of everyone the case agent identified as a victim in the original case against Epstein, with contact and counsel details, and SDNY asks a colleague to make sure the notification database is accurate before the letter goes out. Notification logistics; the list itself is not reproduced. EFTA00025189 (FY 2021 large case-related expenses request form, undated): SDNY estimates a $200,000 request for database hosting and discovery for the Maxwell investigation, estimates at least 50 victims abused by Epstein in New York, Florida and elsewhere, several of them with Maxwell's help, and says the office is considering civil forfeiture actions against Epstein properties worth more than $100 million. A funding request's estimates; it does not show that any forfeiture action was filed.

v3.78 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 41).
