She says she has not met or interviewed any victim in the case, has not treated any Epstein victim or spoken publicly about him, knew of the case from news coverage, a documentary and a podcast before being retained, and was asked to avoid media coverage. Witness-preparation notes of general opinions, not case findings; the expert is not named. EFTA00026939 (contract awarded March 8, 2021): SDNY retains the same trauma-psychology expert for the Maxwell trial, with an estimated performance period to December 31, 2021, at $450 an hour for an estimated 50 hours of preparation and 50 hours of testimony, $45,000 in all, to explain grooming, delayed reporting, attachment between abusers and victims, and the effects of abuse on memory. A procurement record; the contractor is not named. EFTA00027360 (memorandum opinion and order dated March 22, 2021, Dkt. 169): Judge Nathan denies Maxwell's third bail motion. She finds that offers to renounce French and British citizenship are of unclear legal effect on extradition, citing conflicting views of French law, and that an asset monitor with co-signing authority would still leave Maxwell about $450,000 for living expenses plus other assets enough to flee; she repeats her concerns about candor on assets, while finding Maxwell is not a danger to the community. The order as filed. EFTA00027440 (SDNY emails dated Dec 8–9, 2020): prosecutors circulate a draft victim-notification letter, to go out through the notification system, saying the office intends to make a felony plea offer to a woman not yet charged, inviting victims to give their views to the prosecutors by a set date before any offer is made. The draft deliberately omits any reference to the CVRA because other Department components were litigating, before the en banc Eleventh Circuit, whether the CVRA applies before charges. A draft; the woman is not named and whether the letter was sent is not in this document. EFTA00028048 — An October 1, 2020 prosecutors’ draft alleges that an unnamed former assistant arranged appointments involving minors, handled payments and offered incentives not to cooperate with law enforcement. Draft allegations, not findings. No identity is inferred or linked to another entry.


v3.79 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 42). EFTA00029538 — An undated Government proffer describes expected victim testimony concerning Maxwell’s alleged role in recruitment and abuse. Expected testimony is not a finding. The victim’s age, personal chronology and identifying itinerary are omitted.
EFTA00029966 (Government letter filed Aug 13, 2020, Doc 41 in 20 Cr. 330): the Government opposes Maxwell's request that it name certain victim-witnesses 11 months before trial as premature, saying it produced more than 12,000 pages on August 5, 2020 and about 150,000 more pages, mainly financial records, shortly after, and had given the months and years of birth of the three indictment victims; it voices concern that defense counsel referred in a public civil filing to sealed criminal discovery; and it says BOP had not yet put her in general population for safety and security reasons but would give her access to discovery from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily. The Government's positions as filed. EFTA00030379 (emails dated Jul 8, 2020): SDNY sends the Pretrial Services officer assigned to interview Maxwell and prepare her bail report the Government's detention memorandum and the superseding indictment; Pretrial Services says the interview request has gone to MDC and the report should be ready for the court date then set for July 14, 2020. Logistics; officers are not named.

v3.80 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 43). EFTA00030569 (Government letter dated Oct 28, 2020 answering the defense's Oct 13, 2020 discovery requests): the Government says it knows of no statements by Maxwell to law enforcement beyond those at her arrest and in civil cases, no prior arrests, and no items seized from her; that identities and full birth dates of the Minor Victims are premature; that it is not a party to the NPA but will search material from the Florida office for impeachment or witness statements; that it has produced every page of the diary and every version of a requested manuscript it holds; that it holds no compensation-program submissions; that about 62 devices from Epstein's properties are being processed for production by November 9, 2020; and that the grand jury, empanelled in White Plains in November 2019, had no remote participation. The Government's positions as written. EFTA00030638 (emails dated Nov 2–3, 2021): while exchanging draft jury instructions, defense counsel tell SDNY they will keep using the alleged victims' names in drafts and object to calling them 'minors' and 'victims'; SDNY says this forces it to redact every defense filing and risks a victim being exposed by mistake, and considers asking the defense to note its objection in a footnote or else going to the Court. Each side's position as written; counsel are not named. EFTA00030852 (FedEx invoice dated Oct 14, 2002, account in Epstein's name): shipments from October 2 to 9, 2002 between Epstein's New York office and his Palm Beach residence, with one package listing Maxwell as the sender. A billing record; it shows shipments, not their contents, and addresses are not reproduced. EFTA00030893 — Counsel’s February 2021 correspondence submits material for investigators and asks about potentially relevant photographic evidence. The correspondence does not establish that the sought evidence was recovered. Victim descriptions and identifying circumstances are omitted.
EFTA00031173 (emails dated Nov 26, 2021): the SDNY press office reports that a UK outlet said it planned to publish an article using a pseudonymous trial witness's real name and a photograph, and that the office declined to comment; the press guidance circulated to UK reporters says witnesses testifying under a pseudonym should be referred to only by it, regardless of earlier identification, and urges outlets to respect their privacy. Press-office emails; the outlet and the witness are not named here. EFTA00031357 — An anonymous statement presented at Maxwell’s July 14, 2020 bail hearing alleges Maxwell assisted Epstein and expresses concerns about flight and witness intimidation. The declarant’s personal and family history is omitted. Allegations in the statement are not findings.
EFTA00031454 — An August 16, 2021 administrative request seeks travel for trial preparation and support for a victim-witness. Family composition, travel dates and identifying circumstances are omitted. A request does not establish that the travel occurred.
EFTA00031821 — A December 2020 victim statement submitted through counsel opposes Maxwell’s renewed bail application and alleges abuse. Personal history is omitted. The statement’s allegations are not findings.
EFTA00031918 (Maxwell reply dated Mar 16, 2021 in support of her third bail motion, Dkt. 160, with a French lawyer's opinion dated Mar 14, 2021): the reply lists the package — $28.5 million in bonds, $9.5 million in property, $550,000 in cash, an asset monitor who is a retired federal judge, renunciation of British and French citizenship, extradition waivers, home confinement with GPS and private security — and argues the Court keeps jurisdiction despite her pending appeal. It says the Government conceded it cannot show one accuser travelled or had sex acts with Epstein while a minor, and that two counts are New York misdemeanours. The attached opinion disputes the French ministry's March 9, 2021 letter, arguing that a person who has given up French nationality is no longer protected from extradition. Defense arguments, not findings; the Court denied the motion on March 22, 2021 (EFTA00027360).

and EFTA02726638 (173 pp., overlapping copy of the same Day 9

v3.2 (WS2) extension — unsealing appeal resolved: Second Circuit summary order, October 19, 2020 (EFTA00018289, 5 pp.): Case 20-2413-cv — AFFIRMED the district court's July 23, 2020 order unsealing certain litigation materials, including Maxwell's April 2016 deposition transcript. Maxwell appealed, arguing a lower presumption of access for deposition materials than for summary-judgment materials (Brown v. Maxwell, 929 F.3d 41 (2d Cir. 2019)) and that her interests outweighed the public's; the panel (Cabranes, Pooler, Raggi) affirmed. This resolves the unsealing appeal whose July 23, 2020 order and July 29, 2020 reconsideration denial are already in v3.1. Supporting: October 19, 2020 email forwarding "Maxwell_Civil_SO.pdf" — "the same panel just affirmed [the] unsealing of Maxwell's deposition" (EFTA00027066). Reconsideration denied, July 29, 2020 (EFTA00024875, 4 pp.): Judge Preska's Memorandum & Order (Doc 1079) denying Maxwell's motion for reconsideration of the July 23, 2020 unsealing decision — reconsideration is an "extraordinary remedy," granted only on an intervening change in law, new evidence, or clear error/manifest injustice. Unsealing objections (EFTA00022960, 20 pp.): Maxwell's objections to unsealing docket entries 143, 173, and 199 and to unsealing entries 164 and 230 "at This Time" — the objections leg of the same unsealing fight.

v3.2 (WS5) extension: EFTA00092753 / EFTA00097376 (DS9, Jan 2, 2015): Ross Gow's Maxwell statement ("Alan Derschowitz is involved… which he denies") — duplicate filings of one statement responding to the Jane Doe #3 filing. Press-response leg; Maxwell's position via her agent. HO 6005–6020 cluster (HO, Dec 2018–Jan 2019): the People v. Epstein sex-offender-registration (SORA) appellate-brief unsealing fight: NY Post reporter Susan Edelman requesting the DA's appellate brief (HO 6005–6006); the DA's affirmation in response to a non-party motion to unseal (Dec 28/31, 2018; HO 6008–6011); Martin G. Weinberg emails re the motion to unseal (Dec 27, 2018–Jan 3, 2019; HO 6013–6014); Davis Wright Tremaine letter (Jan 4, 2019; HO 6016). DOJ-overlapping: the index number (30129/10) appears in 11 DOJ docs including P1 anchor EFTA00184224, so this is a DOJ-overlapping leg, not an HO-only item.

v3.5 (WS4) extension: (a) Complaint, filed Sep 21, 2015, Doc 1 (EFTA00015726, DS8, 12 pp.): defamation suit against Ghislaine Maxwell; "This suit arises out of Defendant Maxwell's defamatory statements against Plaintiff… [plaintiff] was a victim of sexual trafficking and abuse while she was a minor child" (plaintiff's name redacted in the text layer). (b) Maxwell's Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion to Dismiss Complaint, filed Dec 1, 2015, Doc 15 (EFTA00595583, DS9, 29 pp.): self-defence privilege, pre-litigation privilege, failure to plausibly plead defamation. (c) USAO (S.D. Fla.) letter, Apr 13, 2016, from U.S. Attorney Wifredo A. Ferrer to Laura A. Menninger, filed Apr 19, 2016 as Doc 103-2 (EFTA00703620, DS9, 3 pp., read in full; also filed as 15-cv-07422 Doc 102-7): the Southern District of Florida was recused by the Department of Justice "from prospective responsibility for any criminal investigation or potential prosecution relating to Jeffrey Epstein's alleged sexual activities with minor females" and "was also recused from any criminal investigation of Ms. Maxwell or anyone else relating to those allegations"; Ferrer was "personally unaware of any pending criminal investigation of Ms. Maxwell by any other authority" (not to be construed either way); and "the name Ghislaine Maxwell does not appear in [the Non-Prosecution Agreement], as already reflected in public filings involving that document." (d) Plaintiff's Redacted Motion for Leave to Serve Three Deposition Subpoenas by Means Other Than Personal Service, filed May 25, 2016, Doc 160 (EFTA00617951, DS9, 12 pp.): the three persons to be subpoenaed — Jeffrey Epstein and two redacted names — "were each involved in the sexual abuse and sexual trafficking at issue"; Epstein and one other "have evaded attempts to personally serve them" and have attorneys not authorised to accept service. (e) Response to Motion to Compel Attorney-Client Communications and Attorney Work Product Materials, filed Jun 1, 2016, Doc 184 (EFTA00623075, DS9, 40 pp.). (f) Jeffrey Epstein's Motion to Quash Trial Subpoena (EFTA00589467, DS9, 8 pp., read in full): Epstein, a non-party, subpoenaed to testify at trial Mar 13, 2017, moves to quash; deposed Nov 10, 2016, he asserted his Fifth Amendment privilege to approximately 600 questions; the Court ruled Feb 2, 2017 (under seal) that his privilege assertion was valid and proper as to the questions the parties sought to compel him to answer; his position is that requiring him to appear in person to re-assert the privilege before the jury would add nothing, and would generate "substantial media attention" and impose an undue burden (he resides in the Virgin Islands). The motion's own filing date and docket number are not in the text read — filed before the Mar 13, 2017 trial date. Outcome not in this document. (g) Julie Brown and Miami Herald Media Company's Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion to Intervene and Unseal, filed Apr 6, 2018, Doc 936 (EFTA00805407, DS9, 21 pp.). (h) Emery Celli letter for Intervenor Prof. Alan M. Dershowitz, Dec 3, 2018, Doc 956 (EFTA00802948, DS9, 3 pp.): alerts the Court that materials subject to its protective and sealing orders were allegedly leaked to the press by persons associated with Roberts (the plaintiff), repeating "provably-false and defamatory" allegations against Dershowitz; asks for an immediate conference. Examined, not proposed: Doc 1078-5, filed Jul 29, 2020 (EFTA00084366, DS9, 161 pp.) — Exhibit E, a Jan 18, 2020 press clipping about a new accuser / Interlochen suit; a secondary source, not an atlas anchor.

And if you have a few minutes, let's speak tomorrow." Attachment: "Letter to AUSA _Production_ in _ Response_ to_Subpoena.pdf" (EFTA00091270). Closed-date verification was attempted by page image in v3.5 (WS5) and is NOT possible from the produced documents: the Account Number column is covered by solid black redaction bars in all three copies of the letter (EFTA00065864, EFTA01252357, and the copy attached to EFTA01273238) — the numbers were redacted before production, not lost to OCR — so duplicate-holder rows cannot be matched to specific statement bundles. **No per-account closed dates are asserted.** The table's opened/closed dates, statuses, account types, and authorized signers as printed are confirmed from the images and agree with the text-layer transcription (34 rows); the two Little St James rows opened 7/16/1998 and 1/22/2004 read 'Information not available' for authorized signature. Both carry the same flight-manifest-review paragraph (verified in full context): Maxwell on 16 flights, another person on 80 flights (names redacted/garbled), "the name of Alan Derschowitz" on one manifest, "and a separate manifest with an individual with the name 'Barok' who traveled with two body guards." v3.3 (WS3) extension — the "Barok" two-guards fact gains a dated flight-log counterpart (shared with Story 13): the five copies/variants of one flight-log entry in the compiled Epstein flight/call timeline spreadsheet (DS10) — EFTA01699932, EFTA01702692, EFTA01711655, EFTA01718740 (100 pp., 100 pp., 100 pp., 50 pp.), plus a fifth copy, EFTA01718251 (76 pp., Dec 14 row garbled in the text layer) — each contains exactly one "Barok" occurrence, all the same entry: Dec 14, 2004, 10:12 PM — "Epstein's Flight departs from PBIA (Gulfstream G-1159B)", passengers: Jeffrey Epstein, "Jenn Katlin", "Barok", "1 SS Secret Service", "1 SS Secret Service", "1 Female", "1 Female". (The inbound leg, Dec 13, 2004, 6:11 PM arrival at PBIA, is a separate row — its passenger list also names Katlin.) What this adds: the FBI EC's undated "Barok … two body guards" manifest now has a dated flight-log counterpart — Dec 14, 2004, with two "SS Secret Service" travelers in the passenger list, matching the two-guards shape. What it does NOT establish: (a) the identification of the passenger "Barok" as Ehud Barak is a **candidate, not confirmed** (Standard §6) — the name is spelled "Barok" in both sources, and the "SS Secret Service" rendering is itself odd for a private citizen's travel in Dec 2004 (Barak then held no government post), which is a reason for caution, not for confirmation; (b) the **destination is not established** — the page images of two copies (EFTA01718740 p. 29; EFTA01702692 p. 64) show the spreadsheet has NO destination column at all (columns A–F: Date | Time | Event | From | To | Call length/message info/Passengers; From/To are call fields, empty for flight rows); the return leg (Dec 17, 2004, 10:35 PM) arrives back at PBIA with only Epstein listed (EFTA01718740 reads 'PBIA' cleanly; 'PAM' in EFTA01699932 and 'PSIA' in EFTA01711655 are OCR renderings of the same return airport, not a destination); where the aircraft went Dec 14–17 is not in the spreadsheet, and no tail number appears in any document read, so no FAA/flight-record check is pursuable from this material; (c) the second passenger's NAME is now established as **"Jenn Katlin"** — the page images read "Jenn Katlin" (EFTA01718740 p. 29) and "[first name redacted] Katlin" (EFTA01702692 p. 64); the text layer's "Kollin" and "Jenn Kaffir'" were OCR garbles of "Katlin", which also appears as a passenger on Oct 2, 2004 (EFTA01718251) and on the Dec 13, 2004 inbound leg ("Kalin", EFTA01702692 p. 64). **Who Jenn Katlin is is NOT established** — "Katlin" occurs in exactly 2 corpus docs, both this spreadsheet; no identification is claimed. None of the five Bates is in v3.2; "G-1159B" and "Dec 14, 2004" are likewise absent from v3.2; the four docs contain no other "Barak"/"Ehud"/"Israel"/"Putin" token. Cross-reference: P7 (flight-log family).

v3.5 (WS3) note — a tension in the record: the Cohen itinerary's return (main 19004, PNR 7HLSOQ) departs Dec 14, 2014 via Miami→London→Tel Aviv, while the Baraks' stated plan was to leave Dec 15 at 2 PM to NY (Nili, Dec 7, 2014, main 18310) and their departure is recorded as Dec 15 (EFTA00356456). extensions_v310.text: Direct primary-order verification of an already mapped event, not a new litigation episode. EFTA00013944 (2 pp., Aug 21, 2008, Doc. 26, 08-80736) is Marra's Order to Compel Production and Protective Order itself. It grants production of the NPA, modifications and addenda to petitioners' attorneys, with nondisclosure conditions; counsel must provide the order to their clients and obtain acknowledgments before showing or discussing the terms, and other identified victims requesting access must likewise accept the protective terms. The order was previously recited in the government's opposition (EFTA00204641) and linked to the Aug 14 hearing; this pass supplies its operative text. This is restricted-access production ordered, not public unsealing or proof that the ordered production and acknowledgments were completed. P1's Apr 15, 2021 stopping point and probable tier are unchanged.

extensions_v311.text: Notification ethics inquiry and a bounded disclosure exchange, within the existing CVRA thread. EFTA00014016 (3 pp., Sep 18, 2008) is the AUSA's request to Florida Bar ethics counsel for guidance after a civil attorney alleged that victim-notification letters violated solicitation rules; the request describes separate routing for known represented recipients and asks how to handle letters not yet distributed. These are the requesting lawyer's account and legal position, not findings of compliance. EFTA00014011 (3 pp., Nov 4, 2008, inquiry 28386) supplies the response: Assistant Ethics Counsel Gail Ferguson declines the requested opinion because it concerns past conduct and legal questions about federal statutes and a court order, beyond the authorized ethics-opinion scope. The letter discusses solicitation, represented-party contact and obedience to court orders conditionally; it is neither ethical clearance nor a disciplinary finding. Separately, EFTA00014033 (1 p., Dec 9, 2008, America/Denver MST) records an AUSA email stating that the NPA is attached for Jack Scarola, restricting further disclosure to persons who have signed the protective order; Scarola replies that he will follow the instructions. This documents a particular attachment-transmission statement and reply, not verified completion of all court-ordered production or acknowledgments, inspection of the attachment, or public unsealing. It supplements, rather than reverses, v3.10's order-versus-compliance distinction. P1 remains probable with the Apr 15, 2021 stopping point unchanged.

The CVRA case expanded from two petitioners to four by the January 2015 motion; the court's ruling on the motion is not in the documents read. v3.3 (WS1) extension — Wild decisions + joint statement + notification record (record extended to Apr 15, 2021): *In re Wild*, 994 F.3d 1244 (11th Cir. 2021) (en banc, Apr 15, 2021) (EFTA00074599, 69 pp.) — held the CVRA "did not create a private right of action authorizing a crime victim to file stand-alone civil lawsuit to enforce CVRA rights"; petition denied; district court had found a CVRA violation (359 F. Supp. 3d 1201) but after Epstein's death the requested remedies were denied and the action dismissed (41 F. Supp. 3d 1321); dissent by Branch, J., joined by Martin, Jill Pryor, Hull, JJ. May 28, 2020 — email re *In re Wild*, 955 F.3d 1196 (11th Cir. 2020) (panel) (EFTA00016451, DS8, 1 p.): CVRA rights "do not attach until criminal proceedings have been initiated against a defendant, either by complaint, information, or indictment"; because the government never filed charges and entered an NPA, "the CVRA was never triggered." Joint Statement of Undisputed Facts (CVRA case) (EFTA00191264, 132 pp.) — stipulated facts: (1) between ~2001–2006 Epstein "sexually abused [and] enticed into prostitution minor girls" at his West Palm Beach mansion and elsewhere, incl. Jane Does #1 and #2; §2422 violations; (2) 2006 FBI opened the investigation at PBPD's request; girls 13–17; (4) Jun 7, 2007 FBI hand-delivered a CVRA victim notification letter to Jane Doe #1 promising "best efforts" incl. "reasonable right to confer" and "to be reasonably heard at any public proceeding… involving plea"; (5) Aug 11, 2007 same for Jane Doe #2; (6) Jane Doe #2 was represented by counsel paid for by Epstein; "openly hostile to the investigation… told investigators that she was not a victim… Epstein was an 'awesome man'… would consider marrying Epstein… actively avoided law enforcement… contacted other potential witnesses and victims to advise them against cooperating." (The text layer shows strike-throughs — a redlined draft of the joint statement; cite the stipulated facts as stated.) DRAFT government reply to petitioners' summary-judgment motion (EFTA01100373, 5 pp.): "Any failure to notify or consult were not the result of any 'conspiracy' with JE, nor any bad faith by the Government: they were the result of the USAO following the nationwide DOJ policy" reinforced by a Dec 17, 2010 OLC memorandum opinion (CVRA rights attach when criminal proceedings are initiated; cease if charges dismissed or government declines to bring formal charges after complaint); CVRA amended May 29, 2015 (§3771(a)(9) — right to be informed of a plea bargain/deferred prosecution agreement; "still does not clearly require CVRA rights to apply in the absence of a federal plea agreement or in circumstances where there is a federal Non-Prosecution Agreement"). A DRAFT — cite as the draft reply's argument. Nov 27, 2007 — Jay Lefkowitz (Epstein counsel) → USAO (EFTA00210517, 1 p.): objects to victim notification under the Justice for All Act; §2255 is a civil remedy, not restitution; "we had offered to provide a restitution fund for the alleged victims in this matter; however that option was rejected by your Office" (Epstein's side offered a restitution fund; USAO rejected it, per the letter); requests postponement of notification until after the plea + Starr/Fisher meeting. Jul 2008 USAO email production (EFTA00179991, 168 pp.): Jul 18, 2008 — "our victim notification letter has been filed in court… About 10 letters have gone out so far. The FBI's victim coordinator is updating the addresses on the rest and they will go out on Monday." Aug 1, 2008 — victims' counsel → USAO (EFTA00014125, DS8, 2 pp.): proposes stipulations for the CVRA case: (3) the NPA precludes federal charges for federal sex crimes against the victims; (4) the NPA "was negotiated… in September 2007 (and amended twice more during that year), the victims and their attorneys were not told about the non-prosecution agreement until after June 30, 2008, because of an express confidentiality provision in the agreement that the U.S. Attorney's Office, the FBI, and other federal agents all complied with." Also: Jul 9, 2008 AUSA sent a victim notification to Jane Doe #1 via Edwards. Jul 19, 2011 — USAO (Ferrer) → Roy Black (EFTA00205954, 1 p.): on Jul 17, 2011 the Office received a written request from the Manhattan DA for a copy of the signed NPA + the list of identified victims; per 5 U.S.C. §552a(b)(7) the Office intends to disclose to ADA Deborah L. Morse at 5:00 p.m. Jul 21, 2011; notice per NPA terms. Sep 26, 2011 — the set-aside debate (EFTA00205768, shared with Story 2): internal USAO thread re CVRA relief — "Setting aside the non-pros and prosecuting him as though the Non-pros had never been signed"; the Jane Does' desired relief was to set aside the NPA. Sep 2008 — "Respondent's Opposition to Victims' Motion to Unseal Non-Prosecution Agreement" (EFTA00204641, DS9, 7 pp., shared with P30): the NPA "was never filed in the instant case by the United States, either under seal or otherwise"; Aug 14, 2008 telephonic hearing; Aug 21, 2008 Order to Compel Production and Protective Order (DE 26); the government advised the court the Agreement had three parts: (1) Sep 2007 NPA, (2) Oct 2007 addendum, (3) a letter from the US Attorney to Epstein's attorneys suggesting a further modification; Epstein's attorneys contended the Agreement comprised only parts one and two.

The reply says the petition could cover three different victims: one not fully identified until after the agreement was signed, one whose notification had produced defense claims of prosecutorial misconduct, and a third still being checked. Internal emails. EFTA00014001 (internal emails dated Jul 11–14, 2008): the Government's lawyer reports on the 45-minute July 11, 2008 hearing before Judge Marra. Petitioners' counsel argued for consultation and setting aside the agreement. The Government argued that CVRA rights do not accrue until charges are filed and that the court lacked power to set aside a non-prosecution agreement. The court asked about the gap between September 2007 and the June 30, 2008 plea, ordered the Government's response and declaration unsealed, treated the matter as no longer an emergency, and let the parties confer on factual disputes. One side's account of the hearing. EFTA00014082 (declaration of the line prosecutor, July 2008): she states that the Palm Beach police sought federal help because of concerns about how the State Attorney's Office handled the case; that victim notification letters went out as victims were identified; that one petitioner-side client had earlier been represented by counsel whose fees Epstein paid; that in October 2007 four victims were contacted by phone about the agreement's damages provisions and that, after defense complaints, the Office stopped informing more victims to protect credibility at trial; that she learned of the state plea hearing on Friday, June 27, 2008 at about 4:15 p.m. and called petitioners' counsel; and that one client was left off the list because her prior statements meant she could not in good faith be named in an indictment. The prosecutor's sworn account. EFTA00013570 (Doc 19, entered 08/01/2008): beyond the filing record already carried, the petitioners' response asks for immediate judgment that their CVRA rights were violated, production of the agreement, and production of the report of an October 26, 2007 FBI meeting with Jane Doe #1. It says January 2008 letters telling victims the case was 'currently under investigation' misled them, and says Jane Doe #1 and Jane Doe #2 intended to sue Epstein within days. The petitioners' advocacy. EFTA00010474 (FLSD 08-80736 Doc 205-2, filed 07/05/2013, Appendix B): the United States' sealed motion to dismiss the CVRA petition for lack of standing and ripeness. It recounts that on December 10, 2010 the SDFL U.S. Attorney met Jane Doe #1 and her counsel (Jane Doe #2 declined), that SDFL was later recused and responsibility moved to the Middle District of Florida, and it attaches a limited-disclosure order for the 2005–2007 grand jury materials. The Government's filing. EFTA00010542 (FLSD 08-80736 Doc 462, entered 06/24/2019): the Government's response on remedies, filed by special attorneys from the Northern District of Georgia. It says the government 'should have communicated' with victims more transparently and regrets falling short. It proposes a meeting between victims and a Justice Department representative, a public hearing for victim-impact statements, and CVRA training for SDFL prosecutors. It opposes partial rescission of the agreement as legally barred and harmful to some victims, reporting that more than a dozen victims had invoked the agreement in anonymous civil settlements. It opposes an apology order, disclosure of grand jury and FBI files, damages and fees, and attaches a May 7, 2019 standing invitation to meet. The Government's position.

v3.72 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 35). EFTA00014116 (emails dated Aug 1–2, 2008): forwarding petitioners' counsel's latest letter, which asks the Government to agree two facts about the deferral agreement and why victims were not consulted, the line prosecutor writes that victims were not consulted (apart from the FBI agents' meeting with one victim in September 2007) because the Office did not believe the CVRA applied. The U.S. Attorney replies that the Office also believed contacting the victims would compromise them as potential witnesses, since Epstein argued forcefully that they were 'doing this for the money', and it did not want to discuss liability with them. Internal explanations, not findings. EFTA00014144 (letter dated Aug 26, 2008 from the line prosecutor to Epstein's counsel): she states that the list of 'thirty-two victims' sent to defense counsel on July 10, 2008 is the final list. She says notice of Judge Marra's ruling must go to victims, that the earlier notice language had defense approval although it rested on the December 2007 letter, and that the Office will enforce its right to indict if Epstein breaches the agreement. The Office's position in correspondence. EFTA00014146 (earlier draft of the line prosecutor's July 2008 declaration): compared with the filed version already anchored, this draft dates the FBI victim-witness letters January 10, 2008, says one petitioner-side client was identified in 2007 but refused an FBI interview in October 2007, says pro bono counsel did not report dissatisfaction with the resolution, and states that 'all known victims were not notified' of the June 30, 2008 plea hearing in the time Epstein's counsel allowed. A footnote says letter dates do not show when they were actually delivered. A draft; the wording differs from the sworn version.

extensions_v310.text: EFTA00013590 (1 p., Dec 9, 2008) adds the AUSA's account of a call with the work-release supervisor: paperwork showed a late-September release date based on statutory gain time, while the supervisor reportedly described July 23 eligibility because work release earned an additional two days off per week. The email circulates a draft letter for review. This is a contemporaneous relayed eligibility calculation, not a jail credit ledger, a court ruling, proof that every projected credit was earned, or proof of release on July 23. It supplements P2's existing Dec 8 work-release notice without resolving the final supervision discharge terms or changing the stopping point. P2 remains separate from Story 2's declared NPA-breach thread.

extensions_v311.text: EFTA00014026 (2 pp., Dec 30, 2008, including a Dec 29 exchange) adds the AUSA's explanation of GPS exclusion zones to civil counsel. According to that explanation, Epstein was supposed to travel directly between jail and work, but a route deviation would not itself trigger an alarm unless it entered a programmed exclusion zone. The AUSA relays Captain Sleeth's assurance that identifying location information would not be provided to Epstein and says the zone radius is not known to the writer. This is a contemporaneous explanation of monitoring limits, not GPS telemetry, proof of an actual detour, proof a particular location was programmed, or evidence that every request was implemented. No victim location is reproduced. The v3.10 eligibility calculation remains a projection rather than proof of actual release; final supervision discharge remains unverified. P2 stays separate from Story 2, with its open-at-2010 stopping point and probable tier unchanged.

In 08-80811 (C.M.A.): Epstein's reply re the stay, May 13, 2009, Doc 81 (EFTA00201284, DS9, 7 pp.). Judge Marra's order requesting the United States' position on the stay motions, May 14, 2009 — filed in 08-80893 as Doc 57 (EFTA00234817, DS9, 4 pp.) and in 08-80119 as Doc 99 (EFTA00067377, DS9, 4 pp.; same order, two cases): Epstein "moves for a stay until the expiration of the [NPA]… because… the USAO has taken the position that he is violating the NPA by defending the civil actions"; the Court asks the United States for its position within 15 days, "if possible." The United States' response, May 29, 2009, Doc 121 (EFTA00222205, DS9, 17 pp.). Order setting a hearing on the stay motion (DE 65 in 08-80119) for Friday, June 12, 2009 at 10:00 a.m. before Judge Marra, May 29, 2009, Doc 126 (EFTA00212886, DS9, 4 pp.) — the hearing "shall be limited to the issue of whether Defendant Epstein's defense of the civil actions filed against him violates" the NPA. **New-case filing legs (all within the 2008–2019 span).** 17-cv-00616 (S.D.N.Y.): complaint, filed Jan 26, 2017, Doc 1 (EFTA00285423, DS9, 21 pp.) — pseudonymous plaintiff v. The same April 16, 2020 thread records internal confusion: an official had told the front office a report of the MLAT was false and then had to clarify. A signed final ("Material_Witness_PA_4.02_Final sigmed.pdf") was circulated for reference June 25, 2020 (EFTA00029796). Follow-up (EFTA00031512, June 26–30, 2020): the State Department asked to modify the confidentiality language; SDNY discussed Touhy/FOIA restrictions on the 302 and notes of any interview ("Absent a court order directing otherwise, the SDNY or FBI will not use or disclose the content of the witness's statements…"); and "The FBI should really understand that any leak of any of this would be pretty terrible." Dated stopping point: June 30, 2020. All conduct assertions are the U.S. authorities' REQUEST language, not findings; Andrew stated "not presently a target"; whether the interview occurred is NOT established in DS8. Coordinator's placement decision (see changelog §1): the MLAT stays an extension of P13/Story 3, not its own story — a separate story would duplicate legs v3.1 already carries (the Nov 6, 2020 MLAT pursuit stated as intent, P13's flag).

v3.3 (WS1) extension — proffer agreement form (meeting NOT established): PROFFER AGREEMENT, stamped 01.14.2019 (EFTA00101307, DS9, 2 pp.): "With respect to the meeting of H.R.H. Prince Andrew Albert Christian Edward, the Duke of York, also known as Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor 'Client' and his attorney… with Assistant United States Attorneys… to be held at the Office of the United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York on ('the meeting')" — **the meeting date is BLANK and no signatures are visible in the text layer.** "THIS IS NOT A COOPERATION AGREEMENT." Terms: the government will not offer the client's statements in its case-in-chief or at sentencing except in a prosecution for false statements/obstruction/perjury, or if the client becomes a fugitive; the government may use information derived from the meeting to obtain leads. **Whether the meeting occurred is NOT established from this document.** Do not cite it as a completed meeting.

v3.5 (WS1) extension — DS8 metadata-only survey. 1 leg; predates the Apr 3, 2020 MLAT request already carried. EFTA00022989 (Jan 10, 2020): SDNY notes from a call with Prince Andrew's counsel — requesting a voluntary, consensual interview: not recorded/videotaped, agents take notes, not under oath but lying to federal agents is a crime; subject matter = the nature/scope of Andrew's relationship with Epstein and associates incl. Maxwell; Andrew's status described as "subject" — "sometimes the case that individuals are a subject by default until there is sufficient information to classify them as a witness"; "working on this request for approximately the past month"; parties agreed to be in touch in coming days.

v3.27 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00026542 (2 pp.; header dated Fri, 03 Jan 2020 15:30:01 +0000, as printed): on Jan 2, 2020 SDNY prosecutors email Gary Bloxsome of Blackfords LLP asking him to confirm that he represents HRH the Duke of York. He confirms the representation and asks what specifically they want to contact him about. EFTA00026609 (2 pp.; header dated Wed, 15 Apr 2020 21:48:25 +0000, as printed, forwarded "without comment"): a New York attorney had said in December 2019 that he had been asked to try to act as Prince Andrew's New York counsel. He now reports that his March 2020 emails to the two British lawyers he understood to represent the Prince drew no substantive reply. In December 2019 an AUSA had told him the office could not discuss hypothetical representations. His opinions about the Prince and Maxwell are an outside lawyer's assertions and are not carried. Neither document shows any meeting, proffer or response on the merits. Story 27's carried v3.2 text describes a Gary Bloxsome as Interlochen's counsel, while this document names a Blackfords LLP partner of that name as the Duke's solicitor. Whether these are the same person, or whether the Story 27 attribution needs correcting, is not resolved here. There is no identity merge and no silent fix; the point is flagged for review.

v3.30 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00028001 (1 p.; header dated Mon, 10 Feb 2020 23:37:41 +0000, as printed) is a Feb 10, 2020 internal summary prepared on request. It says that after the U.S. Attorney's Jan 27, 2020 public comments about Prince Andrew, the team heard from counsel for several witnesses who had seen the remarks and sought confirmation that their communications with the team would stay confidential. It also describes pending interview arrangements and a possible attorney proffer for witnesses. The witnesses are not identified here. This is the team's own account of reactions. It is not a finding about the remarks' effect, and it does not show that any interview or proffer took place.

v3.31 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00028560 (2 pp.; header dated Mon, 08 Jun 2020 18:34:56 +0000, as printed): on Jun 8, 2020 an SDNY prosecutor sends U.S. Attorney Berman a short proposed statement responding to a press release issued that morning by Prince Andrew's counsel. The proposed statement says the Prince has never sat for an interview with federal authorities, has repeatedly declined requests to schedule one and, months earlier, said through the same counsel that he would not come in, and that SDNY's doors remain open. Berman asks for a 2:15 call and a dial-in is circulated. This is a draft and SDNY's own characterization of the contacts. It does not show that any statement was issued in this form or that the call took place. EFTA00028760 (2 pp.; header dated Fri, 03 Jul 2020 14:42:01 +0000, as printed) forwards the DOJ London attaché office's Jul 3, 2020 roundup of UK front pages after Maxwell's arrest, including a Daily Mail item saying the Prince is 'bewildered' by a lack of response from U.S. officials while U.S. prosecutors say he declined to schedule an interview. This is a press summary. It reports the newspapers' claims and is not a finding about any contact or about Maxwell's charges.

v3.32 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00029649 (2 pp.; header dated Tue, 03 Dec 2019 13:51:39 +0000, as printed): on Dec 3, 2019 an SDNY AUSA asks the DOJ attaché at the U.S. Embassy in London for a call to ask logistical questions for the Epstein investigation. The attaché replies that there has been considerable UK news about FBI/DOJ interest in Prince Andrew and offers afternoon windows. This is a request for a call and the attaché's reference to press coverage. It does not show the call took place, what was discussed or any contact with the Prince.

v3.51 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 14). EFTA00018922 (Metropolitan Police letter dated 9 December 2019, as printed, with covering email at EFTA00018920): replying to a request made through the U.S. Embassy in London, the Met's Deputy Assistant Commissioner for Specialist Operations gives the U.S. Attorney contact details for the solicitor acting for Prince Andrew in connection with United States v. Epstein, 19 Cr. 490, 'for your information'. The solicitor and firm are not named here. The atlas already records a January 2020 confirmation naming a different firm; whether that reflects a change of representation is not resolved here, and no merge is made.

v3.53 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 16). EFTA00019885 (letter dated Feb 14, 2020 from the Duke of York's London solicitors, forwarded within SDNY): the solicitors say the Duke set out to assist after DOJ first sought his help on Jan 2, 2020; that SDNY confirmed he 'was not and is not a target'; and that the U.S. Attorney's Jan 27, 2020 public statement led to untrue press reports of 'zero co-operation'. They complain that SDNY refused to apologise and went back on a promise about interview arrangements, and conclude that they 'cannot advise the Duke to speak to prosecutors' who cannot be trusted to treat him fairly. Advocacy by the Duke's solicitors; SDNY's response is not shown here. No individual solicitor is named here.

v3.57 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 20). EFTA00022351 (U.S. Embassy London press digest dated Jun 9, 2020, forwarded by DOJ's attaché office): the digest reports that the Duke's legal team said he had offered to speak to U.S. authorities 'on at least three occasions this year' and that DOJ had confirmed he 'is not and never has been a target'. It also reports a Justice Department response that he had sought to 'falsely portray' himself as willing to participate and had 'repeatedly declined' to be interviewed. These are newspaper accounts relayed by a press digest, not the statements themselves; the February 2020 solicitors' letter already anchored (EFTA00019885) is left as is.

v3.58 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 21). EFTA00022980 (emails dated Jan 2–28, 2020, between SDNY and the Duke of York's UK solicitors; individual lawyers are not named here; the Feb 14, 2020 letter is at EFTA00019885): on Jan 2, 2020 SDNY asks whether the firm represents the Duke and requests 'a consensual, voluntary law enforcement interview' about his relationship and communications with Epstein and his associates and certain allegations. The solicitors reply that he has 'a strong desire to cooperate fully' and need at least two weeks for preliminary issues. SDNY asks again whether he is willing to speak, separate from a general desire to cooperate. After the U.S. Attorney's Jan 27 remarks, the solicitors call press reports of 'zero co-operation' and 'no response at all' inaccurate and ask DOJ to make no further public statements; SDNY answers that the U.S. Attorney's statement was factually accurate. Both sides' positions as written; this is an earlier leg to EFTA00019885, not a correction.

v3.79 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 42). EFTA00030190 (SDNY and embassy emails dated Jun 16, 2020, forwarding the January–February 2020 correspondence with Prince Andrew's solicitors): SDNY agrees that the embassy official handling the matter may raise the request with the Home Office on the office's behalf instead of SDNY writing its own letter; the official says the process began in late 2019, that a senior embassy officer had made calls in November or December, and that an earlier solicitor email should not be shared without checking first because it could be cited as a reason the U.S. cannot be trusted. Internal planning; officials and counsel are not named, and no outcome is in this document.

stories.entry_markdown:
Span: Aug 14, 2019–Jan 3, 2022.
Anchors: EFTA00032382, EFTA00027109 (Aug 14, 2019 subpoenas to Noel's
counsel); EFTA00009747 (indictment, Doc 1, filed Nov 19, 2019 — six
counts, 18 U.S.C. §§ 371 and 1001(a)(3), falsified SHU count/round
certifications Aug 9–10, 2019; no counts or rounds conducted ~10:30 p.m.
Aug 9–6:30 a.m. Aug 10); EFTA00017935 (DOJ charging release, same day);
EFTA00009767, EFTA00009775 (the falsified Aug 9/10 SHU check sheets
themselves); EFTA00027732 (Dec 31, 2019 Rule 16 discovery letter —
SHU footage, OCME report, 30-minute round reports, July 23 incident
reports, witness 302s); EFTA00027307 (Apr 24, 2020 government memo
opposing Thomas's motion to compel); EFTA00031263 (same memo, range D
copy — indictment recited, Thomas addendum account); EFTA00031575
(Thomas motion to compel, Apr 10, 2020); EFTA00032687 (Thomas
deferred-prosecution addendum — his account: overtime shifts, fell
asleep, woke ~5:00 a.m., found Epstein hanging, performed CPR;
counsel's argument that MCC staffing culture "encouraged and required"
the behavior, labeled as such); EFTA00028582, EFTA00029061 (May 20–21,
2021 — deferred prosecution agreements entered: defendants admit they
"willfully and knowingly completed materially false count and round
slips," 100 hours community service, OIG cooperation, six-month
supervision); EFTA00013389 (SDNY internal May 20, 2021 urgent report,
same terms); EFTA00031435 (Discovery Production 7, Apr 14, 2021).
Endpoint: nolle prosequi filed Jan 3, 2022 (EFTA00009791, Doc 65) —
deferral expired Nov 20, 2021; Pretrial Services reported both
defendants complied. The indictment is the charge as filed, not a
finding; the DPA admissions are the defendants' own acceptance as
stated in the agreements. FLAG RESOLVED in v3.0 (WS5): the indictment was FILED Nov 19, 2019.
Nov 14 is the date the May 2021 UMR gives for USAO-SDNY having
'obtained' the indictment (EFTA00029061) — a different event in the
charging sequence (grand-jury return), not a competing filing date. The
indictment itself was filed Nov 19, 2019 (EFTA00009747, stamp on all 20
pages; EFTA00017935, 'filed today'; EFTA00031263). The two dates
describe different steps, not a conflict. Note: range C's line 82
('indictment obtained Nov 14, 2019', citing EFTA00027109) is a
misattribution of source, not of date — EFTA00027109 is the Aug 14,
2019 subpoena email to Noel's counsel and contains no November date. EFTA00014985's
text varies from EFTA00009747 ("slept"; 10:30 p.m.–6:30 a.m. window) —
whether it is a superseding version was not established.
Links: 4 (this is its criminal accountability leg); P18 (the
prosecution gated the FOIA release).

v3.0 DS11 extension: EFTA02730000 and EFTA02730002 (May 24, 2021)
— threat-assessment request chain: a threat received May 24, 2021
('THIS ISN'T OVER!!'), forwarded via the attorneys for one of the
Epstein guards (the FBI supervisor's note: 'The victim is one of the
Epstein guards'; the forwarded message is addressed to Tova [Noel]);
the FBI is asked to conduct a threat assessment, with a possible
nondisclosure-order question to the court ('Do you want an NDO on
this?'); the message notes 'Her plea to the DP is tomorrow'. The
threat's source and credibility are not established in the documents
read. (Date note: the DPAs were entered May 20–21, 2021 per Story 24;
the 'plea to the DP is tomorrow' line is quoted as written, not
reconciled.)

v3.2 (WS2) extension — the OIG close-out (shared with Story 4; full text in Story 4's entry above): EFTA00035907 (Jul 15, 2024 BOP status update on the OIG final report dated Jun 26, 2023). Supporting legs: May 21, 2021 email forwarding the draft DPA letter to OIG — "We do not plan to make mention of a report, although if asked at a court conference whether there will be a report, we plan to say that we don't know, and that OIG's normal process is to prepare a report but we don't know wh[ether…]" (EFTA00028580); MCC direction to make daily contact with Officer Noel and inquire about her well-being, August 14, 2019 (EFTA00036379).

v3.2 (WS5) extension: EFTA00124206 (DS9, 130 pp): JPMorgan Chase subpoena response, Dec 18, 2019 (National Subpoena Processing; FBI, 26 Federal Plaza): "Case Name: TOVA NOEL, MICHAEL THOMAS; Case No.: 2019R01059; JPMorgan Chase File No.: SB1089950-F1." The guards' bank-records subpoena production.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — deferred-prosecution recommendation (endpoint unchanged — mid-span leg): "Deferred Prosecution/Misdemeanor Request Memorandum, United States v. Tova Noel, 19 Cr. 830" (EFTA00089488, 16 pp., ~Mar 2021 — undated in the text layer; references Noel's pregnancy due late Apr 2021, C-section scheduled Apr 1, 2021). The case team's recommendation: the Sep 25, 2019 prosecution memo had recommended deferred prosecution ("close case") but "that recommendation was not adopted at the time." With new information — Noel's claim she intended to do the counts/rounds but her co-defendant refused to assist and BOP regulations barred doing them alone; a Western District case where non-prosecution agreements were offered to correctional officers who falsely represented completing SHU rounds when an inmate homicide took place; the Hernandez (N.D. Tex.) precedent; collateral consequences — "we no longer view this as a 'close case,' and believe a felony disposition is not necessary or appropriate… a deferred prosecution is appropriate, and… a felony conviction would be unnecessarily punitive." Recommends "a diversionary disposition… particularly if it included a requirement that [Noel] meet with the DOJ-OIG and provide information about the circumstances that led to Epstein's death." Also: likely sentence on conviction would be probation; "non-trivial litigation risk at trial"; Noel's background (Army National Guard, Kuwait 2012, John Jay 2017, MCC from Jun 24, 2018, mandated overtime, threats from inmates). The memo recommends DP; whether DP was granted is NOT established in this memo (the DPAs were entered May 20–21, 2021 per Story 24's existing anchors).

v3.5 (WS1) extension — DS8 metadata-only survey. 6 legs. EFTA00029992 (Oct 10, 2019): AG Barr SDNY visit briefing — MCC-Epstein investigation: 40+ witnesses interviewed in two months (27 MCC employees, 16 MCC inmates); MCC + financial records reviewed; guards' cellphones searched; dozens of hours of recovered videotape; findings — Thomas and Noel did not conduct the 12 a.m./3 a.m./5 a.m. counts nor most 30-minute rounds; no prison official observed Epstein from ~9:30 p.m. Aug 9 until discovery ~6:30 a.m. Aug 10; falsified forms. EFTA00036602 (Aug 10, 2019): draft press-release note — "the Attorney General has requested that the DOJ Office of Inspector General look into the matter as well" (no AG→OIG wording found in v3.4 by grep). Reyes cluster: EFTA00032297 (Aug 13, 2019 — prisoner production request: Efrain Reyes proffer, Aug 16, 2019, 11 a.m., 500 Pearl/40 Foley); EFTA00019925 / EFTA00017827 (Nov 30, 2020 — Efrain Reyes died, "in his sleep," possibly drug-related per the writer; "we didn't need his testimony" / "you didn't expect to need him for anything Epstein/MCC-related"); EFTA00030097 (Dec 21, 2020 forward of the Reyes thread — same-class, not separately carried). **Identity caveat (v32-ws2 §5, preserved):** whether this Efrain Reyes is the same man as Epstein's Aug 9, 2019 SHU cellmate is NOT established by these documents. EFTA00023092 (filed May 25, 2021): Deferred Prosecution Agreement, U.S. v. Michael Thomas, 19 Cr. 830 (AT), Doc 56 — the DPA document itself (the indictment Nov 19, 2019, six counts, recited; DPAs entered May 20–21, 2021 per Story 24's existing anchors).

v3.7 extension (Grok Bot, DS8 Bates-neighbor survey). 1 leg, 2 documents; endpoint unchanged. EFTA00027731 (Dec 31, 2019): U.S. v. Noel discovery production letter with a replacement attorney's-eyes-only page. EFTA00031434 (Apr 14, 2021): U.S. v. Thomas discovery production 7. Process only.

v3.25 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00024475 and EFTA00024477 (Jul 14, 2020 MDT, America/Denver): an FBI Violent Crimes Task Force agent sends an SDNY AUSA an attachment titled "Initial Review of Records", described as the place in the agent's case file where the phone number and last call made by Epstein were documented. The AUSA forwards it for the MCC shared drive, noting that the team is getting the FBI case file and will need to review the 302s and make discovery decisions. The attachment's contents are not in the text. This is a file-transfer and planned-review step. It does not establish the call, its recipient, or any discovery decision, and it is not merged with the Story 4 August 10, 2019 call relay beyond a cross-reference.

v3.26 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00024810 (1 p.; header dated Fri, 21 May 2021, as printed) is the Public Corruption Unit chief's request, on the day of the planned public letter about deferred prosecution agreements with the two guards, for help reaching the DOJ-OIG lawyer responsible for the report on Epstein's death. It says the guards had agreed to sit for interviews with SDNY and DOJ-OIG and that the team would like the letter to say the interviews would occur as part of an ongoing OIG investigation expected to lead to a public report, but only if DOJ-OIG is comfortable with that representation. This is a request and a proposed representation, made before the carried same-day leg in which the draft letter omits any mention of a report. It does not show OIG's answer or the letter as filed. EFTA00024984 (1 p.; Nov 23–24, 2021 headers, as printed) circulates for review a draft nolle memo for Tova Noel and Michael Thomas with exhibits, including the signed May 25, 2021 deferred-prosecution documents, the committee memos and a draft nolle application and order; a reviewer volunteers to review it. These are drafts in review. The carried Jan 3, 2022 nolle endpoint (EFTA00009791) is unchanged.

v3.27 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00025442 (1 p.; header dated Mon, 27 Jul 2020 12:00:39 +0000, as printed): an AUSA recalls that during MCC employee interviews one or more people mentioned a sign posted in the SHU telling staff to do their checks on Epstein. The AUSA believes the sign was not recovered then and notes that a recent BOP FOIA production included an attached item. An OIG agent and an FBI agent each reply that this is the first time they have seen the sign, and the OIG agent will check the 302s and MOIs. The attachment is not in the text layer. These are recollections and a request to check records. They do not establish the sign's wording, when or by whom it was posted, or that any witness described it. EFTA00026565 (1 p.; header dated Thu, 01 Oct 2020 15:10:22 +0000, as printed): while preparing the latest MCC discovery production, AUSAs discuss unlabelled interview notes of unknown origin and a supplemental FBI 302 about Epstein's arrest. One proposes producing the 302 because it discusses suicidality, but sees no basis to obtain and produce other Epstein files, and another agrees. This is an internal view on discovery scope. It does not show what was produced or any court ruling on scope.

v3.28 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00027153 (1 p.; header dated Fri, 16 Aug 2019 00:51:57 +0000, as printed): on Aug 15, 2019 an SDNY AUSA sends a colleague, following an earlier conversation, the charging instruments from a Northern District of Texas case and the Fifth Circuit opinion affirming the conviction, under the subject "MCC/Epstein - Prior 1001 Prosecution". The attachments retained alongside include a 2014 N.D. Tex. indictment captioned United States v. Frederick Hernandez et al. (EFTA00027136, partial, caption only relied on) and a 2013 N.D. Tex. information (EFTA00027134, partial). This places a reference to a prior correctional-officer false-statement prosecution five days after the death. It is an earlier leg of the carried Hernandez (N.D. Tex.) precedent, and it is not a charging decision. EFTA00027028 (2 pp.; outer header dated Thu, 09 Jul 2020 14:30:49 +0000, as printed): in response to a Jun 12, 2020 request for policies, logs and lists from the time of a defendant's SHU assignment, an MCC investigative agent sends what he has. On Jun 24 he says he could not locate watch calls or SROs from the requested period. He was told that SROs were likely not completed then, and that most original Control Center paperwork, including watch call sheets, was seized by the FBI and/or OIG shortly after the incident. An AUSA notes that BOP's "hot lists" production contains other inmates' confidential information, that Epstein was never placed on that list, and proposes simply saying so. These are BOP-side accounts and an internal discovery proposal. They do not establish what was seized or completed, the list's contents or what was produced.

v3.31 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00028709 (2 pp.; header dated Fri, 21 May 2021 20:37:01 +0000, as printed) supplies the reply missing from the carried May 21, 2021 leg. After the Public Corruption Unit chief's request and a draft letter that cites the DOJ-OIG review but does not mention a report, a DOJ-OIG official answers that OIG has no objections. The draft explains that if asked in court whether a report will issue, the team plans to say it does not know and that OIG's normal process is to prepare a report without knowing whether it will be public. EFTA00028699 and EFTA00029187 carry the same chain with brief thanks and are not separate anchors. This is OIG's no-objection reply to draft language. It is not the letter as filed, a commitment to a public report or the report itself.

v3.32 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00029280 (3 pp.; header dated Wed, 27 Nov 2019 17:32:56 +0000, as printed) is a Nov 21–27, 2019 FBI thread on video status. An FBI agent preparing for discovery says the government will turn over all available SHU-area footage on CH0082, CH0080 and CH0062. She asks what drive capacity is needed, how many cameras DVR1 has, and whether a correct camera-location list exists, saying the lists she has seen were wrong. She also says a system failure stopped DVR 2 recording, so there is no footage on it after July 29. FBI technical staff reply that DVR 2 was not worked on because the dates fell outside the team's dates of interest. They say its data might be recoverable only through a long project, likely 6 or more months, with no guarantee, and that it would need a formal EC request. These are the agents' and technicians' statements. They are not a forensic audit, a recovery attempt or a finding about missing footage. They sit alongside the carried EFTA00017948 'DVR 2 not running' account in Story 4 without merging with it.

v3.33 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00029999 (1 p.; header dated Fri, 11 Oct 2019 17:55:31 +0000, as printed): on Oct 11, 2019, under the subject 'Epstein MCC CO charges', an ODAG staff member forwards to SDNY a question received earlier that day: 'When is SDNY planning to indict?' This is a question passed on, not a charging decision. It predates the carried Nov 19, 2019 indictment and leaves it unchanged. EFTA00030148 (3 pp.; header dated Thu, 26 Dec 2019 13:37:54 +0000, as printed) is a Dec 20–26, 2019 thread between SDNY and counsel for a person who had met with the Office; the person's name is redacted in the text. SDNY plans to produce redacted notes of that meeting to defense counsel under the protective order, and the person's name on an attorneys'-eyes-only basis. Counsel proposes further redactions or a sealed application to Judge Torres to preclude the disclosure. In counsel's view, the client is not a witness, the material is not Brady material, and the statement was an error that the surveillance video contradicts. SDNY says it cannot agree to the redactions and suggests a sealed motion, ex parte as to the defense. On Dec 26 SDNY lists three corrections to counsel's draft letter. The thread does not name the case. It is placed here because of its timing, the Judge Torres references, the defense production and the surveillance-video reference, and that placement is a judgment, not a documented link. Counsel's characterizations are counsel's own. The letter is a draft, and nothing shows a filing, a ruling or a production. No officer is identified.

v3.35 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00031081 (3 pp.; header dated The, 19 Nov 2019 14:58:51 +0000, as printed): on Nov 19, 2019 a reporter forwards to SDNY, where it is circulated internally, a press release from Senator Ben Sasse issued that morning on the arrests of two of Epstein's prison guards. The release calls the arrests important but not the end and lists the senator's earlier letters and statements. It is a senator's public statement, not a DOJ position, a charging document or a finding. EFTA00031449 (1 p.; header dated Wed, 14 Apr 2021 21:12:22 +0000, as printed): on Apr 14, 2021 SDNY AUSAs send a colleague the deferred-prosecution memos for the two defendants, with the application materials, for comments and edits, and add a dated memo attachment for one of them. The memos are attachments not in the text layer. This is a circulation of drafts for review, not an approval or an agreement. The carried May 2021 agreements (EFTA00028582, EFTA00029061) and the earlier memorandum EFTA00089488 are unchanged.

v3.41 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 4). EFTA00013214 (email dated Sep 25, 2019): a timeline report of the DOJ OIG Cyber team's forensic examination of the two computers retrieved from the SHU is circulated; a prosecutor calls it underwhelming and asks for copies of the documents Thomas opened at the start of his shift. The report itself is an attachment not read here.

v3.61 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 24). EFTA00025239 (opening read only, of the Government's Rule 16 discovery letter dated Dec 31, 2019 in U.S. v. Michael Thomas, 19 Cr. 830; transmittal EFTA00025238): the first production, under the Dec 16, 2019 protective order, includes MCC surveillance footage of the SHU common area from 7/5/2019 to 8/12/2019 (SDNY_00000001), which a footnote says the Government seized on or about Aug 10, 2019, and commissary records for MCC inmates (SDNY_00000002–00000020). Only the opening of the letter was read; the rest of the production list is not represented here.

v3.63 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 26). EFTA00027031 (emails dated Dec 20, 2019): counsel for an individual who met with SDNY, who counsel says is not a witness, propose a redacted disclosure and cover letter modeled on one the Government used in another SDNY case, as a way to 'ensure our client's safety' while the Government meets what it believes are its disclosure obligations. As an alternative, they offer to apply under seal to Judge Torres for a protective order precluding disclosure. They argue the material is not 3500, Rule 16 or, in their view, Brady material, but 'an error made by our client that we understand is contradicted by the surveillance video evidence'. SDNY replies that it will review and respond. Counsel's position only; the individual, the statement and the outcome are not identified here.

v3.65 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 28). EFTA00028324 (emails dated Jun 23–30, 2020; companion EFTA00028317): in guard-case discovery, the prosecutors ask BOP 15 questions about what it produced, and an MCC staff member answers. Lieutenants' logs exist only digitally and are emailed to executive staff every 24 hours; the 'SHU Logs' are the digital log books for the evening and morning watch. The 'Hot List' is BOP's only high-risk list, and the one produced is dated August 30, 2019, after the events. The respondent knows of no BOP or MCC policy on cellmate assignments. The psychology suicide-prevention slides used in quarterly SHU training are dated 6/11/13 (an inmate version 1/2/2014). Watch-call sheets were 'reportedly seized' early in the investigation, and Epstein's central file may have been taken after his death (unconfirmed). Prosecutors ask for high-risk lists from June 26 to August 10, 2019 and narrow the SRO request to Epstein only. BOP-side answers as written; the staff member is not named here.

v3.66 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 29). EFTA00029185 (urgent report text dated May 20, 2021): SDNY reports that it plans to offer deferred prosecution agreements to the two MCC correctional officers indicted in November 2019 for falsifying count and round forms on the night of Epstein's death. Terms: cooperation with the pending OIG investigation, admission of guilt to the indicted conduct, 100 hours of community service, six months of pretrial supervision, and no new crimes; BOP administrative action is not precluded. Its stated rationale is the interests of justice, the defendants' mitigating personal circumstances, and the Department's practice 'in the overwhelming majority of other cases' involving falsified count or round forms. It says the outcome is supported by OIG and the FBI and approved by Pretrial Services, with a public letter planned by May 21 and entry expected by May 28. SDNY's internal rationale as written; the officers are not named here.
