stories.entry_markdown:
Span: Dec 2010–Nov 2020.
Anchors: EFTA00019480 (Dec 10, 2010 Cassell asks SDFL U.S. Attorney
Ferrer to investigate "the most suspicious criminal case I have ever
encountered"; May 6, 2011 OPR declines on grounds of ongoing
litigation; Feb 7, 2019 Cassell asks OPR to keep victims informed);
EFTA00015719 (Feb 6, 2019 — DOJ opened an investigation into Acosta's
role in the 2008 plea deal at Sen. Sasse's request after the Miami
Herald's "Perversion of Justice" series; OPR to head it);
EFTA00018568 (Aug 6, 2020 — OPR sends SDNY its 380+ page draft report
on SDFL's 2006–2008 handling, plus ~30-page appendix); EFTA00020454
(Dec 8, 2020 — Relativity processing report on the OPR materials:
300,123-doc set, 5,462 with hits); EFTA00011475 (Nov 2020 Executive
Summary, 14 pp.; duplicate EFTA00013359, 13 pp.).
Endpoint: Nov 2020 OPR Executive Summary. Findings as stated in the
summary: OPR did NOT find professional misconduct by Acosta or the
other subjects in resolving the investigation through the NPA, and did
not find evidence the decision was based on corruption or impermissible
considerations such as Epstein's wealth, status, or associations;
Acosta resisted defense efforts to return the matter to the state and
refused to eliminate incarceration and sex-offender registration;
the Oct 2007 "breakfast meeting" did not lead to the NPA, signed weeks
earlier. OPR DID conclude Acosta exercised poor judgment in resolving
the federal investigation through the NPA ("a flawed mechanism for
satisfying the federal interest") and poor judgment in failing to
ensure victims were notified about the state plea hearing. The full
OPR report is not in DS8 — only the executive summary and the draft's
processing trail; findings are reported as the summary states them.
Links: 1 (the NPA under review), 2 (breach/inaction), P1 (CVRA).

v3.2 (WS5) extension: EFTA00038270 (DS8, Sep 2, 2020): DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility letter (950 Pennsylvania Ave.) to the FBI, re the OPR investigation.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — interview transcript + intake + jurisdiction (span unchanged, Dec 2010–Nov 2020; the Apr 2008 item below is a prologue leg, not a span move — coordinator's decision, see changelog §8): OPR interview of R. Alexander Acosta, Oct 18, 2019, Washington, D.C. — 412 transcript pages across four Bates ranges: EFTA00009229 (DS7, 100 pp., pp. 1–100), EFTA00009329 (DS7, 99 pp., pp. 101–199), EFTA00009116 (DS7, 113 pp., pp. 300–412) (pp. 200–299 = EFTA00009016, already WS5-sampled and Story 1-anchored as DS1-8). Acosta is told he is a subject: OPR is investigating (1) whether prosecutors committed professional misconduct by entering the NPA, and (2) Judge Marra's Feb 2019 finding that the government violated the CVRA. Passages read: Acosta on witness assessment ("these girls are young. They're impressionable. They are scared. Will they stand up in court?"); on balancing ("we also thought it was very important that he serve some real punishment, and that he register… a lot of people are going to be questioning for a long, long time, but that's how we balanced it"); on the CEOS critique relayed by OPR counsel ("I'm not thrilled about the agreement… Epstein is getting a much better deal than the average defendant… I would have taken the guy to trial unless the victims were clearly against it"). Read at head/tail depth, not cover-to-cover. Jan 4, 2011 — "Call from OPR" (EFTA00206528, DS9, 1 p.): OPR is in "preliminary stages of determining whether the matter should be opened into an investigation" re Cassell's request; OPR asked for (1) memos/emails showing the decisional process for entering the NPA, including opposing views, and (2) documents showing whether the FBI was made aware of the NPA negotiations (Cassell claims the FBI was kept completely out). The OPR intake leg. Apr 21, 2008 — AUSA's OPR self-report of conflict of interest (EFTA00208240, DS9, 3 pp., prologue leg): during pre-indictment plea negotiations the AUSA provided Epstein's counsel a series of possible attorneys for victims' civil-damages counsel, including Humberto Ocariz, "a friend of my boyfriend" (later "a friend of a close friend"); Epstein's counsel selected Ocariz; after conferring, the office decided it should not select victims' counsel and a Special Master (pro bono) would; Ocariz was NOT selected. The AUSA self-reports the allegation. The memo also narrates Operation Leap Year background: 25+ minor victims identified; PBPD → State Attorney → FBI → USAO; state grand jury indicted only 3 counts of solicitation of adults; indictment package prepared; counter-proposal (state plea + sex-offender registration + jail + damages); Acosta meeting; appeal to Washington (2 weeks); two-track drafting (NPA + federal plea agreement/information). Aug 24, 2020 — OPR planning to invite all known Epstein victims to a meeting "in order to announce the results of OPR's investigation into SDFL's non-prosecution agreement with Epstein" (EFTA00032211, DS8, 1 p.). Jan 29, 2019 — OIG letter (Horowitz) to 15 House members (EFTA00811997, DS9, 2 pp.): OIG does NOT have jurisdiction over DOJ attorneys' litigation/legal decisions; exclusive jurisdiction is OPR (IG Act §8E(b)(3)); OIG has objected to this limitation for 30 years. Explains why OPR, not OIG, investigated the NPA. Note: the OPR Executive Summary copies (EFTA00011475 / EFTA00013359 / EFTA00023059 / EFTA00095558 / EFTA00095727 / EFTA01250797 / EFTA01726257) are multiple copies of one summary; EFTA00011475 + EFTA00013359 are already Story 25 anchors. The summary's findings as read: all five subjects did NOT commit professional misconduct re the NPA's development/negotiation/approval; BUT OPR concludes Acosta's decision to resolve the investigation through the NPA "constitutes poor judgment" ("a flawed mechanism for satisfying the federal interest"); Acosta exercised poor judgment in failing to make certain the state would notify victims about the state plea hearing; victims "were not treated with the forthrightness and sensitivity expected by the Department."

v3.4 (WS4) extension — referral, inquiry, declination, public statement (span unchanged, Dec 2010–Nov 2020): Dec 16, 2010 — USAO → Cassell/Edwards (EFTA00208288, DS9, 2 pp.): Cassell's Dec 10, 2010 request for an investigation "has been referred to the Department of Justice's Office of Professional Responsibility"; the USAO is seeking DOJ guidance on whether it can continue to defend the CVRA case, and a recusal "would likely ensue"; the USAO cannot answer Cassell's request that the government concede CVRA non-compliance and set-aside relief. May 3, 2011 — Cassell/Edwards → USAO re Reinhart's motion to intervene (EFTA00205035, DS9, 4 pp.), with the enclosed OPR chain (Mar–Apr 2011): the complaint was opened "as an inquiry and assigned for review. It is not an investigation"; OPR "takes no position regarding any party's representations in litigation"; it is "unusual for OPR to initiate an investigation of matters that have been or could have been raised in litigation." Sep 29, 2011 — Cassell → U.S. Attorney Ferrer (EFTA00205183, DS9, 2 pp.; shared with P1): OPR stated May 6, 2011 that it would NOT investigate Cassell's allegations (issues "being addressed in the court of litigation"); Cassell renews the request and adds an allegation about a named senior prosecutor (name redacted in the text layer; not reproduced here) — Cassell's allegation, labeled as such, not a finding. Nov 12, 2020 — DOJ Office of Public Affairs statement on the OPR report (EFTA00013355, DS8, 3 pp.; EFTA00039868 is the SDNY-forward duplicate): the executive summary "was released today to affected victims"; OPR "did not find that Department attorneys engaged in professional misconduct" but concluded victims "were not treated with the forthrightness and sensitivity expected by the Department" and Acosta "exercised poor judgment" in resolving the investigation through the NPA and in failing to make certain the state would notify victims about the state plea hearing. The public record of the endpoint; span and endpoint unchanged.

v3.5 (WS4) extension: the May 6, 2011 OPR declination in OPR's own words — OPR letter to Prof. Paul G. Cassell, May 6, 2011, filed as 08-80736 Doc 82-1, entered May 16, 2011 (EFTA00806869, DS9, 1 p., read in full): "OPR has completed an inquiry into your allegation" of professional misconduct by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida concerning the non-prosecution agreement ("improper influences"); OPR "declines to investigate" per its policy of refraining from investigating "issues or allegations that were, are being, or could have been addressed in the course of litigation, unless a court has made a specific finding of misconduct" — "Most, if not all, of the allegations… are currently being litigated" in the CVRA case, 08-80736; "No court has made a finding of misconduct and there are no extraordinary circumstances." Story 25 already records this declination via Cassell's Sep 29, 2011 letter (EFTA00205183); this is the primary document behind it.

v3.7 extension (Grok Bot, DS8 Bates-neighbor survey). 1 leg; endpoint unchanged. EFTA00013358 (Nov 13, 2020): an SDNY attorney forwards OPR's public executive summary (justice.gov link) noting it "explains how OPR evaluates things". Confirms SDNY receipt of the summary; adds no finding.

v3.27 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00025398 (3 pp.; outer header dated Tue, 07 Apr 2020 12:44:55 +0000, as printed): OPR asks SDNY which of the individuals it wishes to interview briefly, on limited historical matters, are represented by counsel. SDNY answers on Apr 3, 2020 that of the 32 individuals listed, 22 are represented by Brad Edwards, two by Jack Scarola, and one each by Sigrid McCawley, Rita Glavin and Gloria Allred. Four could not be reached at AUSA level and one is believed deceased. OPR says it intends no interference with SDNY's work. On Apr 6 SDNY raises no objection to OPR asking about past contacts with USAO-SDFL and FBI-Miami in about 2005–2008, but asks OPR to avoid the substance of the underlying conduct and to share any such statements for 3500 purposes; OPR agrees. These are SDNY's stated understanding of who is represented, plus agreed ground rules. They do not show whom OPR interviewed or what anyone said. No individual is identified here.

v3.31 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00028680 (1 p.; letter dated November 12, 2020, as printed) is OPR's transmittal of its Report of Investigation into SDFL's 2006–2008 resolution of the Epstein investigation and its interactions with victims, signed by OPR's Director and Chief Counsel to the Acting U.S. Attorney for SDNY. The letter says that, although the investigation did not involve SDNY, the report is provided because it may be relevant to ongoing litigation handled by SDNY. It also says the Department is publicly releasing the Executive Summary that day, does not plan to release the full report at that time but will provide it to Congress on request, and that parts may become public through FOIA processing. EFTA00028679 is the Nov 12, 2020 cover email, forwarded Nov 16, attaching the signed letter and the report with exhibits; the report attachment is not relied on here. EFTA00029071/29072 stay preview-only as receipt items. These are OPR's statements of its intentions. They do not show congressional receipt, any FOIA release or SDNY use of the report, and they leave the carried Executive Summary endpoint and findings unchanged.

v3.33 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00030290 (2 pp.; header dated Wed, 10 Jul 2019 14:32:24 +0000, as printed): on Feb 12, 2019 an SDNY AUSA introduces herself to OPR as one of the AUSAs on SDNY's current Epstein investigation. She offers to be in touch for any deconfliction or discussion useful to their respective matters. On Feb 19 OPR asks to speak that day, and a call is proposed for Feb 20. On Jul 9, 2019 the AUSA asks to speak again, and a time on Jul 10 is agreed. This is contact and scheduling. It does not show what was discussed or that the calls took place, and it leaves the carried OPR span and endpoint unchanged.

v3.39 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 2). EFTA00024873 (OPR email dated Mon, 27 Jul 2020, in a chain to Jul 28): OPR gives SDNY's public-corruption chief its figures: about 516,000 email files collected for five subjects (mostly from the line AUSA who stayed on the CVRA litigation until mid-2019), about 3,000 unique emails judged directly relevant, and scanned USAO hard-copy sets chiefly from the CVRA litigation; SDNY asks for copies and OPR raises the issues of giving its records for a case in litigation. OPR's estimates; whether copies were provided is not shown.

v3.68 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 31). EFTA00031320 (letter dated February 10, 2019 to the Department of Justice, re: investigation of misconduct in prosecution): a Florida lawyer writes that he represents a longtime associate of Jeffrey Epstein who is willing to testify in the investigation and that the testimony will 'include details of obstruction of justice'. The lawyer discloses that the client is suing Epstein in Florida state court (Miami-Dade case no. 14-21348CA 01) and copies Epstein's lawyer in that suit. An unsolicited offer; the claims are the writer's, and the client is not identified in the text read. The lawyer and client are not named here.

v3.70 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 33). EFTA00032930 (internal email dated Apr 8, 2021, 'OPR and PMRU Stuff'): an SDNY attorney circulates the analytical-framework section of the public executive summary of OPR's Epstein report and the Justice Manual provision (1-4.320) on the Professional Misconduct Review Unit. These say OPR finds misconduct only when, by a preponderance of the evidence, a subject attorney intentionally or recklessly violated a clear and unambiguous standard, and may otherwise find poor judgment. They also say OPR misconduct findings go to the PMRU, which can impose discipline on career attorneys and authorize bar referrals but has no authority over non-career political appointees. Quoted public and policy text; the reason it was circulated is not stated in the text read.

Span: Apr–Oct 2021.
Anchors: EFTA00022706 (Aircraft Purchase Agreement, Apr 2021 —
Hyperion Air sells a used 2008 Keystone/Sikorsky S-76C++, serial
760750, FAA registration N722JE, two Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 engines,
for $1,800,000: $200,000 deposit to escrow, $1,600,000 balance at
closing; second copy EFTA00022696; third copy EFTA00022855);
EFTA00022855 (First Amendment Apr 20, 2021; Second Amendment May 7,
2021 — deposit increased and disbursed to the seller without any
requirement that a closing occur; closing deadline extended to May 13,
2021 as the absolute final date); EFTA00022793 (AIC digital-signature
notices, May 6, 2021); delivery receipt executed (EFTA00022867–EFTA00022868, Exhibit F;
date not legible in OCR — v3.0, WS4) and FAA registration statement
in the purchaser's name filed in the same production set; EFTA00020095, EFTA00022666 (SDNY grand-jury
subpoena to AIC Title Service re N722JE, Sep 30, 2021); EFTA00020098
(AIC production, Oct 11, 2021, sent in six parts).
Endpoint: production completed Oct 11, 2021. The sale is documented
through agreement, both amendments, and delivery receipt (executed;
date not legible in OCR), plus an FAA registration statement in the
purchaser's name filed in the same production set. The closing date
is NOT established: May 13, 2021 is the Second Amendment's
contractual final deadline only, not evidence of when closing
occurred — and the Second Amendment disbursed the deposit without
any requirement that a closing occur. Delivery evidence and closing
date are kept separate (v2.1). Indyke signed for Hyperion
Air as authorized representative — signature only, no wrongdoing implied.
Links: P15 (same airframe family; N722JE is distinct from the S-76D
demo aircraft in P16), P21 (Hyperion Air is a defendant there).

v3.0 DS10 extension (WS3): JPMorgan wires to Hyperion Air Inc — Feb
20, 2003 $100,000 via Citizens Bank DE, IMAD 0220B1OGC01C002838
(EFTA01482357); Jul 21, 2006 $100,000 via Citizens Bank DE, IMAD
0721610GC08C004027 (EFTA01482743); 26 lines, 26 docs, Feb 2003 – Jul
2006. This predates the S-76C++ sale by over a decade and the
slice-DS10 S8 May 2019 closed-account query by 13 years; it is a
funding leg for the same company, not evidence about the sale.
Cross-link: P15.

v3.56 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 19). EFTA00021666 (opening read only, of emails dated Aug 24–Sep 29, 2021, between SDNY and an FAA contact; continuation EFTA00021675): the FAA contact's notes trace the S-76C-2 helicopter, serial 760750. Tail N750A is recorded as sold on Dec 30, 2008 with a Delaware registrant; Air Ghislaine Inc. becomes Shmitka Air Inc. on Feb 11, 2010; the tail changes to N722JE in March 2010; N722JE is registered to Freedom Air International Inc. on Aug 25, 2010; it is sold to ASI Wings LLC under a Jul 26, 2011 bill of sale; ASI Wings sells it to Hyperion Air LLC, St. Thomas, on Jun 13, 2019; and Hyperion Air sells it to Industrial Integrity Solutions Inc. under a May 13, 2021 bill of sale. SDNY plans to contact the title companies next. The FAA contact's notes as written. The signatories are not named here; the 2008 buyer's name is not in the text read.

Span: Dec 11, 2001–Nov 2014.
Anchors: EFTA00016841 (will Dec 11, 2001, 24 pp., with five codicils
2003–2007 — all property to the Trustees of The Jeffrey E. Epstein
2001 Trust; executors Jeffrey A. Schantz and Paul Hoffman, $100,000
each); EFTA00016865 (will Jan 2012, 11 pp. — Trust One; executors
Darren K. Indyke, Joseph Pagano, Lawrence Newman; successors Jes
Staley and Andrew Farkas); EFTA00016876 (will Sep 16, 2013, 8 pp. —
2013 Trust; executors Indyke, Pagano, James E. Staley, $250,000 each;
successor David Mitchell); EFTA00016884 (will Nov 2014, 9 pp. — 2014
Trust; executors Indyke, David Mitchell, James E. Staley, $250,000
each; successor executor Lawrence H. Summers). Each will revokes all
prior wills and codicils; each is a pour-over to a then-current trust.
Endpoint / dated stopping point: Nov 2014 will — the latest will in
the 2001–2014 succession this entry documents. The Aug 8, 2019 will
and the probate opening are documented in DS8 and belong to P24
(EFTA00027979, verified DS8, 21 pp.); the v2.0 DS8-wide claims that
no later will or probate is documented in DS8 are withdrawn (v2.1).
The instruments in this entry are filed here as grand-jury exhibits
(GJ stamps).
FLAG (v3.0, WS5 — CARRIED UNRESOLVED, narrowed): the 2014 will
(EFTA00016884) names "LAWRENCE H. SUMMERS" as successor executor
with no further identifying information — the name occurs once
(Article THIRD A); no address, date of birth, occupation, affiliation,
or other identifier anywhere in the will; the other four wills
(EFTA00016841, EFTA00016865, EFTA00016876, EFTA00027979) contain
zero "Summers" hits. The Larry Summers of P12 presents himself under
the identical full name "Lawrence H. Summers" (Barak 10056,
lhs@lawrencesummers.com; DS11 EFTA02343136, Sep 26, 2014, and
EFTA02540589, Jan 8, 2018, larrysummers.com / @lhsummers),
corresponding directly with Epstein 2013–2018 — the same period in
which Epstein named a "LAWRENCE H. SUMMERS" successor executor (Nov
2014). "Lawrence H. Summers" appears in 487 corpus documents; no
second Lawrence H. Summers appears anywhere in the searched material.
No document states the will's appointee is (or is not) that man —
identity NOT established. A shared exact name (including middle
initial) plus a shared orbit is not an identification under §6. Do
not conflate; do not merge P19's Summers into P12. What would decide
it: a probate filing, executor-qualification paper, or correspondence
naming the successor executor with an identifier; or a document
showing a different Lawrence H. Summers in Epstein's orbit.
Links: P10 (Butterfly trusts — separate trusts, kept distinct); P24
(the 2019 will and probate open).

Span: Nov 25, 2019–Oct 26, 2021.
Anchors: EFTA00027912 (Nov 25, 2019 — Jordy Feldman introduces
himself as co-Designer (with Feinberg and Biros) and Administrator of

Estate"; Dec 2, 2019 plaintiffs' counsel object — decision-makers
selected and hired by the Estate cannot be said to be independent;
Dec 4, 2019 Feldman replies; Dec 9, 2019 Kaplan demands a fourth
administrator selected by plaintiffs and unanimous claims decisions);
EFTA00027884 (Dec 11, 2019 conference before Judge Failla in Jane Doe
v. Indyke, 19 CV 8673 — estate counsel confirms the fund/protocol is
"full steam ahead," no plaintiff had yet agreed to try it);
EFTA00027350 (by Jan 2021 the fund is referenced as a source a
Maxwell-trial witness might draw on for family travel costs);
EFTA00029867 (Jul 13, 2021 trial-prep notes — a witness knows she is
not able to sue Maxwell after participating in the fund);
EFTA00028274 (Nov 8, 2021 defense disclosures list two fund General
Releases among trial exhibits); EFTA00029598 (Sep 2021 — FBI
threat/stalking case opened over a denied fund claim);
EFTA00028032 (Oct 26, 2021 — caller to the USAO victim line reports
she has applied to the fund); EFTA00011028 (protocol draft, Dec 13,
2019); EFTA00010010 (General Release form, Oct 3, 2020, "Exhibit E");
EFTA00037538 (Jun 1, 2020 VI Daily News article carried in FBI thread
— estate proposed the fund Nov 2019; VI AG filed a CICO civil
enforcement action Jan 2020 and placed liens on the $600M+ estate;
"agreement in principle" on fund terms, with reforms, and release of
a portion of estate funds so the program may proceed); EFTA00038885
(Apr 7, 2021 — counsel writes a client filed a claim and had her
interview with the fund managers the previous day).
Endpoint: the program is operating by 2021 — applicants applying,
participants bound by general releases, a denied claim generating a
federal threat case. Dated stopping point: Oct 26, 2021
(EFTA00028032). PROMOTED from v1.5 DS9 fragment ("no
filing→determination→payment arc traced") — the DS8 arc runs from
proposal through the design fight to operation. Probable, not confirmed: no in-range document shows the protocol's finalization or a specific payment determination — the middle of the arc (final protocol → first payments) is inferred from participant/applicant mentions, not directly documented. The program's launch date is now established: Jun 25, 2020 (EFTA00032569, embargoed announcement). The Jan 2024
JPMorgan-fund determinations in P27 are a separate fund.
Links: P3 (the fund is the estate's alternative to civil litigation);
P24 (same executors); 5 (fund releases surface as Maxwell trial
exhibits).

v3.2 (WS2) extension: December 14, 2019 (EFTA00019565, 5 pp.): Roberta Kaplan forwards Jordy Feldman's December 14, 2019 email on the Epstein Victims' Compensation Program to Kate Doniger and Alex Conlon — the design-fight thread continues three days past the December 11, 2019 Failla conference already in v3.1. Filing-leg only; no new protocol term is established from the opening read.

v3.5 (WS1) extension — DS8 metadata-only survey. 3 legs; closes the launch-date gap. EFTA00032569 (Jun 25, 2020): embargoed announcement — VCP commencement: individuals "may begin the process of filing claims"; designed by Feinberg, Biros, Feldman with input from attorneys for 70+ victims, the VI AG, the Estate; administered by Feldman. **Closes the launch-date gap stated in v3.4 P23** ("no in-range document shows… the program's launch date"). EFTA00023230 (Dec 3, 2019): estate counsel letter to McCawley — the program was presented to the USVI court Nov 14, 2019 for approval; estate assets "in excess of $577 million" per the Aug 19, 2019 probate petition. EFTA00011011: co-executors' expedited motion to establish the VCP, USVI probate ST-19-PB-80 — 13 pp. but only 2,692 chars in the text layer (mostly image-only); the motion date is NOT in the text layer; the Nov 14, 2019 presentation date is established via 23230; "To date, twelve lawsuits involving Sexual Abuse Claims have been filed…"

v3.7 extension (Grok Bot, DS8 Bates-neighbor survey). 1 leg plus a date correction. EFTA00032855 (Nov 4, 2019): accepted SDNY calendar entry, location "Epstein / Victim Fund Meet". Correction: EFTA00011011's page image (p. 1) carries a Superior Court receipt stamp reading "19 NOV 14 AM 9:02", so the co-executors' expedited motion was stamped Nov 14, 2019; v3.6 said the date was not established.

v3.15 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00019448 (1 p.; June 2020 Superior Court order, ST-19-PB-80; exact signature day not reliably legible in the text layer) grants the co-executors' motion to establish the voluntary claims-resolution program and authorizes commencement on or about June 15, 2020. The order records the June 1 status report's representation that interested parties had finalized and supported the protocol; its footnote reports an agreement that the USVI Attorney General would lift liens to permit funding. Correction/qualification to the carried P23 gap description: a categorical statement that no in-range document documents protocol finalization is now too broad. This order documents judicial authorization and the co-executors' finalization representation, not the final protocol text itself, executed lien releases, actual funding transfers or an individual payment determination. Authorization on or about June 15 is not actual launch on that date and does not displace the already-carried June 25, 2020 commencement announcement. P23 remains probable, the later operational evidence and endpoint unchanged; it is not merged with the separate JPMorgan compensation fund.

v3.37 extension (ordered DS8 continuation, final actionable slice). EFTA00032718 (2 pp.; header dated Mon, 02 Dec 2019 20:23:13 +0000, as printed): on Dec 2, 2019 an SDNY Civil Division AUSA notes that the U.S. Virgin Islands court had posted the estate's probate petition seeking 'expedited approval' of a victim claims fund (the attachment is named '11.14.2019 Expedited Motion for the Establishment of Voluntary Claims'), more than a week after filing. The AUSA says the posting page is not an official docket, that no complete electronic docket had been found, and that SDNY is inclined to call the court. A colleague forwarding it asks whether a Rule 6(e) application has been drafted. The petition is an attachment not read here. This is an internal monitoring note, not an approval of the fund. The carried June 2020 order establishing the program is unchanged, and the 6(e) item is not merged with the carried P19 December 20, 2019 order.

v3.61 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 24). EFTA00025237 (emails dated Dec 19–30, 2019): an SDNY attorney relays to a supervisor a request from the estate's attorneys to meet a senior office official, which the supervisor will come by to discuss. The attorneys want to 'elevate' the discussion of their proposed plan for a victims' fund, saying it would be in all parties' interests, 'including the victims, to engage in meaningful discussions about a possible resolution'. The estate attorneys' position as relayed; whether a meeting occurred, and the office's answer, are not shown, and the officials are not named here.

v3.52 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 15). v3.55 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 18). stories.entry_markdown:
Span: Feb–Mar 2016 contacts; Apr 2019 ex parte proceedings; 2021 motion practice.
Anchors: EFTA00029077 (Maxwell moves to suppress all evidence
obtained from the Boies Schiller subpoena and to dismiss Counts Five
and Six (perjury) as its fruits, alleging the government misled Judge
McMahon about prior contacts with Boies Schiller and about what it
knew of the file, and that the government had "significant and
substantial contact" with victims' attorneys in 2016; exhibits C–I);
EFTA00028929 (reply, with exhibits J–Q including Feb–Mar 2016 email
strings and handwritten AUSA notes; duplicate EFTA00029100);
EFTA00029540 (Judge Nathan's Apr 16, 2021 Opinion & Order — resolves
Maxwell's other pretrial motions but expressly defers the suppression
motions: "which the Court will resolve in due course"). Background:
during the pending Giuffre v. Maxwell defamation case, a civil
Protective Order barred sharing confidential discovery material
(including Maxwell's April and July 2016 depositions) with the
government; the government issued a grand-jury subpoena for Boies
Schiller's file and applied ex parte before Chief Judge McMahon
(19 Misc. 149); sealed order and sealed memorandum decision Apr 9,
2019; a parallel application to Judge Netburn (19-MC-00179, Apr 16,
2019) was separately rejected, per the defense motion.
Endpoint: motion fully briefed; suppression ruling deferred in-range.
Dated stopping point: Apr 16, 2021 (EFTA00029540). Probable: the
procedural chain is documented, but the load-bearing claim — that the
government misled the court — is a defense allegation in a filing,
not a judicial finding, and the 2016 email exhibits cited are sealed
and were not read. The motion's assertion that Manhattan prosecutors
declined to pursue an Epstein/Maxwell case in 2016 rests on a cited
Oct 13, 2020 New York Daily News report, not on a document in DS8.
Links: 5 (the perjury counts and the 90,000 pages of material at
issue are the Maxwell prosecution's core); 7 (the protective order
and depositions come from the defamation case); 2 (the 2016
declination, if established, would be the bridge between the 2008
NPA era and the 2019 case — NOT established here).

v3.2 (WS2) extension: Netburn application, February 28, 2019 (EFTA00011520, 6 pp.): SDNY's sealed letter to Judge Sarah Netburn with its application and proposed order under the All Writs Act (28 U.S.C. § 1651) for a limited order to unseal discovery materials in Boies Schiller Flexner's possession, in connection with Jane Doe 43 v. Epstein, et al., 17 Civ. 616 (JGK). The government states it served a grand-jury subpoena on Boies Schiller for copies of discovery and related materials in that litigation (investigation into Epstein and others for possible violations of 18 U.S.C. §§ 1591, 1594(c), 2422(b)); Boies Schiller does not intend to contest the subpoena, but believes a protective order in the litigation may preclude compliance. This dates the Netburn application to February 28, 2019 (v3.1 carries the April 16, 2019 rejection per the defense motion). The defense reply memorandum in support of the suppression motion (EFTA00018997, 20 pp.) and the motion to dismiss Counts One–Four as time-barred (EFTA00028903, 22 pp.) are the same motion-practice family already carried under Story 5/P26.

v3.5 (WS1) extension — DS8 metadata-only survey. 2 legs. EFTA00020298 (Apr 27, 2021 order, Doc 252): DENIES Maxwell's Rule 17(c) subpoena to Boies Schiller as to Requests 1–8 and 12; reserves judgment on Requests 9–11; denies the Government's requests; directs the Government to notify the Court of its views on 9–11. EFTA00015865 (May 4, 2021 letter, Doc 269): Government submits Requests 9 and 11 should be denied; reserve decision on Request 10, which may be rendered moot.

v3.18 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00020692 (4 pp.; April 29, 2019 MDT, America/Denver, carrying March 25–April 24 correspondence) adds a record-processing leg for the Boies Schiller subpoena returns. After instructions for first and second production folders, a sender reports that the data has been loaded to Relativity and is available for review. The chain expressly excludes specified DVD structures, original ZIP folders and several PDFs from the requested loading and raises a separate video-format conversion question. The completion statement is bounded by those instructions: it is not a verified load of every produced item, proof of completed substantive review, successful video conversion, public unsealing, protective-order compliance or a judicial finding on the defense's misconduct allegations. It is distinct from the later Manhattan-device/USVI-exclusion loading account and does not resolve the suppression claim or change P26's probable tier or endpoint.

v3.34 extension (ordered DS8 continuation). EFTA00030849 (3 pp.; header dated Thu, 21 Jan 2021 15:12:59 +0000, as printed) is a chambers thread in In re Grand Jury Subpoena, 19-mc-00179, before Magistrate Judge Netburn. On Jul 15, 2020 the courtroom deputy sends an order filed under seal that day. A letter follows in connection with that order, and an endorsed order is sent to be filed under seal. On Jan 19, 2021 a sender submits a letter responding to the Court's Jul 27, 2020 Order and asks that it be sealed, and on Jan 21, 2021 the deputy sends an order filed under seal that day. The orders and letters are attachments not in the text layer, and the senders are not identified. This shows sealed activity on the docket in 2020–21. It does not show what was ordered, and it leaves the carried account of the 2019 application, which rests on the defense motion, and the P26 endpoint unchanged.

v3.54 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 17). EFTA00020697 (emails dated Apr 15–18, 2019; production cover at EFTA00020699): SDNY sends Boies Schiller Flexner a sealed order permitting it to comply with SDNY's grand-jury subpoena, served Feb 5, 2019, by producing discovery materials from the 15 Civ. 7433 litigation. SDNY stresses that the order covers only that case, not other litigation such as Jane Doe 43 v. Epstein (17 Civ. 0616). BSF responds on Apr 18, 2019 with correspondence and a secure link to materials. Lawyers are not named here.

v3.79 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 42). EFTA00029816 (Maxwell memorandum served Jan 25, 2021): Maxwell asks the Court to suppress everything the Government obtained by grand-jury subpoena from the law firm that represented her civil accuser, and to dismiss the two perjury counts. She argues that in the 2019 sealed proceeding before Chief Judge McMahon a prosecutor wrongly said the office had no prior contact with the firm and did not know what its files held, whereas the firm had met prosecutors in February 2016 and later urged a perjury charge; she says she sat for her 2016 depositions relying on the civil protective order, and notes that Magistrate Judge Netburn refused a similar Government request in another civil case. She asks at least for an evidentiary hearing. Defense allegations, not findings; counsel and the prosecutor are not named.

v3.81 extension (DS8 protected pass, cut 44). demands the allegations not be published or disseminated, under threat of
instructing London attorneys to sue. part03:1393 [main 15455] (Jan 5,
2015, Sommerlad→Barak): "We ran your statement in today's paper but did
not name you. You are among many people disputing the account of this
woman. Would you be prepared to meet with a colleague of mine who is in

story?"

Span: Jan 23, 2015 – Mar 13, 2016.
Anchors (part02/part03 IDs): part03:669 (Jan 25, 2015, Jiang
Mianheng→Barak; body quotes the Jan 23 Jiang letter and Barak's Jan 24
reply): Barak and Goldwasser met Jiang in Shanghai "last Monday" (Jan
19, 2015); SAIL point of contact is Xidong Sun. part02:3347 (Mar 16,
2015, Yun Jiang→Goldwasser, Barak CC'd): SAIL delegation's Israel trip
confirmed for May 10–15, 2015. part02:1909 (Apr 11, 2015,
Goldwasser→Barak): tentative itinerary for the SAIL visit to Israel.
part02:490 (Jun 3, 2015, Yun Jiang→Goldwasser, quoting Goldwasser's May
19 letter): both visits confirmed — Goldwasser: "It was a pleasure to
host your team during your stay in Israel"; Jiang: "Last week, Mr. Barak
came to see us in Shanghai. Dr. Mianheng Jiang and Mr. Barak had a
conversation regarding the future collaboration between SAIL and EBG";
SAIL is studying "the first batch of projects we visited in our stay in
Israel" and lists 12 companies. part02:274 (May 28, 2015,
Goldwasser→Kuhn, Barak CC'd): MOU draft prepared at SAIL's request.
part02:341 (Jun 4, 2015, Jiang→Barak, quoting Barak's Jun 4 email):
Barak sends the MOU draft and budget proposal; Jiang: "We will revert
to you when my colleagues complete the review of the MOU."
Endpoint / dated stopping point: Mar 13, 2016 — the last SAIL row in main (main 2613); the arc ends in active dispute over the Side Letter and Advisory Services Agreement, not with a signed deal. The MOU text was agreed Oct 15, 2015 (main 9943, 8927); SAIL signed the MOU Oct 23, 2015 (see v3.4 extension — main 9899; file-level anchor Gmail03/Inbox!7/1 (347)). No Founders countersignature, no signed Advisory Services Agreement, and no payment is in rows read. The Feb 19, 2016 strain note (main 3131 — Barak to Jiang: "I've met several hurdles and obstacles in my relationship with Prof. Goldwasser") is now inside the span, not a follow-up flag. The main-DB follow-up pass is DONE (v3.2 WS3; 140 SAIL rows confirmed exactly). Business / association
record, not an allegation. SAIL = Shanghai Alliance Investment Ltd.,
No. 19 Gaoyou Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai.
Links: 14, 15.
Verification (v3.0, WS2): document-level verified — anchors body-read
in full. New to the atlas, anchored in already-indexed content.

v3.2 (WS3) extension — main-DB follow-up (all anchors body-read in full; 140 SAIL rows confirmed exactly): Sep 6–8, 2015, Goldwasser Shanghai visit — SAIL proposes "both parties will sign the MOU next week when you are at SAIL" (main 7263, Sep 1); SAIL "are interested to try and close the MOU and have it signed by us during this upcoming visit to Shanghai" (main 7393, Sep 3). No row states the MOU was signed in Shanghai in September; negotiation demonstrably continued after the visit (Sep 10 MOU draft, main 7449; Oct 11 SAIL revision, main 8663; Oct 15 updated MOU, main 8927) — so the September signing did not happen, or at least is not documented. Oct 15, 2015 — MOU text agreed, signature pending SAIL internal approval: main 9943 (Goldwasser→Jiang: "we agree to the latest version of the MOU you sent us. If you wish me to sign it and send it to you I will do so. If you first wish to have it approved internally on your side, please let me know when the MOU is approved and signed by you."); main 8927 (SAIL's revisions — SAIL Group definition, the foreign-shareholder clause, exclusivity "in China"; counsel Barasch: "Unless E&Y disagrees, I'd suggest signing as is" — a recommendation to sign, not a signature); main 8951 (SAIL side, Oct 11: "we believe that we are quite close to the goal of signing the MOU"). Oct 25–29, 2015 — SAIL delegation visit to Israel planned (main 9943: arrival late Oct 25, meetings and company visits Oct 26–29, a Weizmann Institute laboratory visit, a tour Fri Oct 30, meetings with the Israeli VC community; earlier main 8834 and main 9140, Oct 8: the delegation had not yet received visas); completion NOT established — no arrival, meeting, or debrief row was found in rows read. Dec 2015 — Advisory Services Agreement + Side Letter drafting; Barak–Jiang telcos: main 4810 (Dec 14, revised draft of the Advisory Services Agreement; "the language in 1.3 and 1.4 reflects the MOU", "the budget was agreed in the MOU", "SAIL says that the term was agreed between E.B. and SAIL's chairman", "E.B. and Benad were removed as parties from the agreement"); main 5017 (Dec 15, Goldwasser wants the revised agreement sent "as soon as possible (today!)" before his Shanghai visit in two weeks); main 4844 (Dec 10, term dispute — Barak and Jiang had agreed in Shanghai in June that the initial term is 3 years, extendable to 5; SAIL says the term is a "key issue"); main 6633 (Dec 27, SAIL sent a "Key Issues List" Dec 24; Goldwasser to fly to Shanghai Jan 3, 2016, meetings Jan 3–6 — the trip's outcome is not in rows read; there are NO SAIL rows at all between Dec 27, 2015 and Feb 23, 2016); main 6353 (Dec 21, Barak↔Jiang telcos Dec 14–21, 2015; Jiang "authorized our team to discuss with Professor [Goldwasser] when they meet early January of 2016 in Shanghai"). Feb 19 – Mar 13, 2016 — strain and dispute at cutoff: main 3131 (Feb 19, Barak→Jiang: "I've met several hurdles and obstacles in my relationship with Prof. Goldwasser"); main 4118 (Feb 23, Goldwasser→Barak: "We are advancing with SAIL towards closing of the fund yet there are open issues between us that we need to resolve" — staffing and a budget adjustment; "I understand that you have reservations."); main 3191 (Mar 10, SAIL's business-issues list on the Side Letter and Advisory Services Agreement — EBG ownership, SAIL: "we have been informed Mr. Barak will own about 20% shares of EBG; and Prof. Goldwasser will have 35-40%" — attributed to SAIL, not verified; non-compete survival; the IP-acquisition model; advisory fees, Q1 $625,000, Q2–Q4 $569,444 each, Year-1 formation costs $166,667 — negotiation figures, not payments; payment timing vs Chinese offshore payment rules; a $2M Year-2 budget with termination as the fallback; Goldwasser's draft replies call SAIL's proposals "offensive, disharmonious and insulting" and invoke "The MOU provided for a firm 3 year commitment"); main 2613 (Mar 13, counsel advises sending the sharp reply only to Dr. Jiang, without CC, so as not to cause him loss of "face"; a Mar 14 conference call was scheduled). Kuhn's role: adviser to Barak/Goldwasser, deliberately unnamed during the MOU process, expecting to oversee China-side JV operations once the MOU was signed (main 7393 and main 9051); Kuhn met Jiang Jun 30/Jul 1, 2015 (main 11670 and main 11769). Tier stays confirmed — the collaboration arc (two completed visits in 2015 + MOU negotiation + definitive-agreement drafting) is documented; the endpoint is now the Mar 13, 2016 cutoff in active dispute.

v3.3 (WS2) extension — MOU drafts now parsed from the mailbox attachments (endpoint and tier unchanged — confirmed; the collaboration arc is documented; the endpoint is the cutoff in dispute, not a signed deal): MOU v1 (May 18, 2015, main 11305, GKH-LAW #5997335v1) — parties: Shanghai Alliance Investment Co. Ltd. ("a private equity and venture capital arm of Shanghai Municipal Government"), Mr. Ehud Barak, Prof. Benad Goldwasser — acting through a company to be established by them ("the Company", later EBG). Recitals: SAIL "desires to dedicate an aggregate of three hundred million United States Dollars (US$300,000,000)" over five years to acquire rights in technologies from Israeli healthcare and life sciences companies ("Target Companies"); §1 "copy paste" model: SAIL or Portfolio JVs acquire **exclusive technology rights in China**, including future developments/improvements and associated production files and technology transfer; China only; Portfolio JVs prohibited from selling products based on the Technology Rights outside China; **no ownership stakes either way**; SAIL's prior consent required for every acquisition. §3 consideration: **3.1** annual fee "[three million United States Dollars (US$3,000,000)]" for an initial five-year Term, based on a pre-approved budget; **3.2** the Company is a founder of each Portfolio JV and receives **20% ownership interest without making any capital contribution**, plus minority protection and anti-dilution rights; **3.3** if SAIL/affiliates/portfolio companies invest directly in Israeli companies during the Term, the Company gets **20% of the profit**; **3.4** if SAIL acquires a company (or its technology) introduced by Barak/Goldwasser, then **[X%] of the total aggregate purchase price** (percentage blank); **3.5** if SAIL enters into any agreement with an introduced company, then **[X%] of the payments** (percentage blank). §5 non-circumvention: Term + 24 months. §6 non-binding: except §§3.3–3.5, 4, 5, 7, the MOU is non-binding; the parties agree to negotiate the Definitive Agreements in good faith within sixty (60) days. §7: governing law Hong Kong; CIETAC arbitration, Beijing, English. **Signature block: date "May __, 2015"; SAIL address blank; Barak's and Goldwasser's Israeli I.D. numbers blank; signature lines and SAIL "Chop" line blank. No signatures, no chop, no date. An unsigned draft.** EY-comments version (May 28–29, 2015, Gmail11/Sent!4/1 (315) — the parent message survives only as the Gmail11 Sent copy, Barak→Nili May 29, 2015; **no main-DB row** — cited as a file-level anchor with that caveat, not as a DB row): Goldwasser forwards Amit Oring's (EY) May 28 email: "Pls find the MOU with our comments. Plus a clean version." Changes vs v1: "Founders" terminology introduced; §2 expanded into "Efforts" (Shanghai travel, board seats, Shanghai tech hub); **annual fee raised $3,000,000 → $4,000,000** (still bracketed as a draft figure); §3.2 reworded to shares-or-option for 20% of each Portfolio JV (zero exercise price); §3.3 narrowed to investments in companies *introduced by* Barak/Goldwasser; new §3.6 (consideration survival); new **§6 Exclusivity: "The Company shall be SAIL Group's exclusive representative in Israel in the healthcare, life science, medical device and pharmaceuticals sectors during the Term."** Signature block again blank. Unsigned draft. SAIL's comments on v19 (Aug 5, 2015, main 8034 — Yun Jiang→Goldwasser; "Attached please find our comments for the draft MOU"): SAIL wants a guarantee that it is EBG's exclusive representative in China in the same sectors; SAIL wants its already-contacted Israeli companies listed as an Exhibit as exclusivity exceptions; **Key Person:** Barak and Goldwasser named as Key Persons, each to "devote substantially their business time and attention to the activity of EBG"; if either ceases to do so (a "Key Person Event"), "the collaboration between the parties shall end."; SAIL proposes EBG introduce **at least 100 projects per year**, paced quarterly; SAIL wants EBG's share (the X% in §§3.3–3.5) set "with the reference of the regular practice in the field", and a **maximum proportion** (cap) stated; SAIL proposes a second structure — Israeli hi-tech companies contribute IP/knowhow to form the Portfolio JV with the Chinese partner — and SAIL/related Chinese companies want to **reserve the right to acquire ownership stakes in the Israeli hi-tech target companies** (against v1's no-stakes rule); the Israeli counterpart should be confirmed as EBG; since EBG "is not formed at the moment", the Founders sign the MOU and assign all rights/obligations to EBG once established; the 60-day Definitive Agreements target is "a tight schedule". The $3M/$4M and 20%/X% figures were internal draft positions — Goldwasser to Kuhn, May 28, 2015 (main 12855): the exact numbers "have not [been] discussed with" SAIL. GKH's engagement proposal for the MOU/definitive-agreement work recorded May 27, 2015 (main 12677). **Signature (CORRECTED in v3.4 — see below):** the v3.3 statement "Signature is still NOT established" is withdrawn as a blanket statement. SAIL signed the MOU Oct 23, 2015; the Founders did not sign that copy. DOJ corpus: "Shanghai Alliance" scores 0 hits; no SAIL MOU material found. Coverage limit carried (v3.3): the Sep–Dec 2015 MOU versions (main 7449, 8663, 8927), the Dec 2015 Advisory Services Agreement drafts (main 4810, 5017), the Key Issues List (main 6633) and Budget_EBG_v3.xlsx (part02:341) sat in Gmail01/02/03/04 zips, which did not survive on disk; their contents were not parsed. **Resolved in v3.4 (WS2):** the zips survive on the Internet Archive (item gmail-06) and the versions were recovered by range-request and parsed — see the v3.4 extension. One file stays unparsed: main 7449's own attachment (the GKH-marked v21), which is not present as a `_files` entry in any zip.

v3.4 (WS2) extension — SAIL attachment parse completed; signature finding REVERSED in part (endpoint and tier unchanged — confirmed; the arc still ends Mar 13, 2016 in active dispute over the Side Letter and Advisory Services Agreement, not with a signed deal). Recovery: the Gmail01–04 zips survive on the Internet Archive (item gmail-06); all six unparsed versions were recovered by HTTP range-request and parsed, except main 7449's own attachment file (the GKH-marked v21), which is not present as a `_files` entry in any zip — its content is substantially captured indirectly via SAIL's Sep 22 comments quoting v21, the SAIL-revised v21, and the Sep 30 comments with Goldwasser's inline replies. **SAIL signed the MOU Oct 23, 2015.** The signed copy is a one-page EasyScan scan (Gmail03/Inbox!7/1 (347) — file-level anchor, no DB row), forwarded by Jiang Oct 23, 2015 ("Attached please kindly find the signed MOU by SAIL. Thank you! I will also bring the original signed file with me to Israel, if necessary.") and forwarded on by Goldwasser the same day ("מזל טוב לנו" — "congratulations to us"); the parent message is indexed as main 9899 (Oct 25, 2015, Barak forward, Hebrew subject). Page-image read of the scan: §§8.5–8.6 and "IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this MOU as of the date first above written"; footer `15332/1001/6116561v5-20151015`, page 5 — the last page of the Oct 15, 2015 v5 MOU. SAIL block: handwritten Chinese-character signature above the line; "By: Mr. CAI, XIAO HONG"; "Title: President" (handwritten); a red round chop (company seal, star in centre). **Ehud Barak signature line: BLANK. Prof. Benad Goldwasser signature line: BLANK.** Whether the Founders ever countersigned — including on the original Jiang offered to bring to Israel for the Oct 25–29 delegation visit — is NOT established in rows read (FTS "countersign": 23 hits, all 2014–Jul 31, 2015, none SAIL-related; "signed MOU" after Oct 23, 2015: only main 9899 itself; no SAIL rows Oct 25–29, 2015 other than 9899). The Dec 2015 Advisory Services Agreement drafts' recital ("the Parties have executed a Memorandum of Understanding on ___, 2015") treats the MOU as executed but leaves the date blank. **MOU economics evolution (parsed texts):** v12 (May 26, 2015, main 12855's attachment) still carries the $300M aggregate and a $4M annual fee with 20% ×2; v17 (Jun 1) and v19 (Jun 2) drop the $300M, set the annual fee = annual budget (initially US$2,500,000), and blank the equity percentage — the big renegotiation happened May 26–Jun 1, 2015, despite main 12855 (May 28) saying the numbers "have not [been] discussed with" SAIL (attribution of the change to SAIL vs the Founders' side NOT established from these files alone). SAIL's Sep 22 comments on v21: the SAIL Group definition (4 entity types); the §3.2 10% formula dispute (draft "X=10%*A+B" vs SAIL's reading "X=10%*A"); minority protection = anti-dilution; Part II — transfer of future earnings to EBG, Goldwasser's other responsibilities to be listed as a Definitive Agreement exhibit, technology-trade as a further co-operation model (proceeds "discussed and determined case by case"). Sep 30 comments with Goldwasser's inline replies ("Benad: That's fine. I asked my lawyers to clarify... except that I replaced absolute holding to majority held..."; "Benad: Yes, that's what was agreed, my lawyers must not have understood me properly" on the 10% formula); SAIL on §7.1 — governing law must be PRC for agreements with state-owned enterprises; §7.2 — arbitration in Beijing in English AND Chinese. Oct 10 SAIL revision (main 8663's attachment): the Oct 15 clean is its restructured successor (SAIL Group definition inserted; §2 Formation of Portfolio JVs with the 10% formula inserted; sections renumbered; "SAIL" → "SAIL Group"; foreign-shareholder fallback to EBG; exclusivity "in China"). **Oct 15 v5 clean** (main 8927's attachment — the version SAIL signed): 3-year term extendable by mutual consent to 5, no $300M aggregate; §2 Founders' equity = 10% of SAIL Group's interest (foreign-shareholder fallback to EBG); §3 EBG screens 100–150 Target Companies/year, presents 25–40/year to a joint committee; Barak Chairperson "dedicate significant time"; Goldwasser CEO "dedicate a majority of his business time"; Key Person — SAIL may end the Term on 6 months' notice if either cannot dedicate the time (softened from the v19-comments "collaboration shall end"); §4 annual fee = annual budget, initially US$2,500,000; §4.2 call option up to 5% of shares held by SAIL Group (6% if exit within 24 months); §4.3 M&A payment 2% up to $100M, 1.5% $100–200M, 1% above $200M; §4.4 other-agreement proceeds "discussed and determined case by case"; §6 non-binding except §§3.8, 4.2–4.6, 5, 7, 8 and §6; Definitive Agreements within 60 days "or as soon thereafter as practicable"; §7 exclusivity both directions; §8 governing law PRC (v1: Hong Kong), CIETAC arbitration Beijing, English AND Chinese. **Advisory Services Agreement drafts (Dec 2015):** Nov 30 SAIL draft (jy-clean) — parties SAIL + Barak + Goldwasser as Founders; Dec 7 v2 (main 4810's attachment) and Dec 14 v4 — parties SAIL + EBG only, Founders removed as parties (matches main 4810: "E.B. and Benad were removed as parties from the agreement"); all three: $2,500,000 annual budget, 3-year term extendable to 5, $166,667 set-up fees, budget Total $2,481,067; all undated, signature pages blank. **No signed Advisory Services Agreement in rows read.** **Key Issues List Dec 22, 2015** (main 6633's attachment, SAIL's side): SAIL will only contract with EBG, not the Founders; Founders want to be contracting parties for recourse ("SAIL cannot only contract with a newly formed entity which gives SAIL limited recourse"); technology rights only for Mainland China, excluding Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan; first-payment dispute — Founders: due in 30 days after signing or SAIL Fund formation, covering two quarters (half of $2.5M) plus $166,667 EBG formation fee, then quarterly at beginning of quarter; SAIL: first installment $1.2M within 60 days after signing; §4.2 tag-along right pro rata, NO blocking right; §6.2 Key Man termination (SAIL pays office rent only if termination is due to SAIL's breach); Exhibit V call option subject to state-owned-assets regulatory requirements, no blocking right, calculation only at Exit event. **Budget_EBG_v3.xlsx** (part02:341): salaries Benad $312,000/yr, Manager $312,000, Barak $312,000, Dan $234,000, Analyst $124,800, Admin $54,600; subtotal $2,314,400; set-up fees $166,667 ("$500K to be divided over 3 years"); Total $2,481,067 — matching the ASA Exhibit III figure to the dollar. The $2.5M annual fee vs $2,481,067 budget leaves an $18,933 gap unexplained in the documents; not reconciled. **Coverage:** the six versions are now parsed (main 7449's file excepted — see above); the Sight Dx / Biondvax presentation attachments (main 6633) are not recovered or parsed — only Goldwasser's Dec 14 email summaries are read; no leg is proposed from them. The Oct 15 revision docx is a tracked-changes version; the clean copy is authoritative and tracked-change extraction was not done.

Span: Apr 22 – Jul 31, 2015.
Anchors (part02 IDs, plus main verification): part02:997 (Apr 27–May 4,
2015, Belyakov→Barak via Nili; Barak's May 1 reply inside): formal
invitation as SPIEF panelist with a program and an offered meeting list
(Kudrin, Shuvalov, Dvorkovich, Sergey Ivanov, Ulyukaev, Nabiullina,
Lavrov). Barak: "I'm planning to come. I'm highly interested in meeting
# 4,6,7, on the list" (Ivanov, Nabiullina, Lavrov) — proposals, not
meetings — "and also anyone of the others that you think is worth
meeting"; notes prior Forums' receptions were "arranged by Yuri
Ushakov's office at the time". part02:1161 (Apr 28, 2015,
Belyakov→Barak, "SPIEF 2015") — same invitation leg. part02:148 (Jun 9,
2015, Kartasheva→Nili): car and driver provided, airport Officials and
Delegations Lounge reception; Barak "placed at the main section for the
Plenary Session with the President of Russia". part02:81 (Jun 9, 2015,
Noskova→Barak): session "Building Effective Cyber Security Systems"
with Barak's participation, Jun 18, 17:00–18:15 — "Please confirm
finally your attendance." (Confirmation of THIS session is not in rows
read.) part02:262 (Jun 10, 2015, Nili→Noskova): "I confirm PM Barak's
participaton in the session Unlocking the potential growth of the
knowledge economy on june 20." Verification (main DB): main 12310
(Jun 25, 2015, Belyakov→Barak): "I hope SPIEF met your and your wife's
expectations and you enjoyed your visit to St.Pete last week!" — post-forum
thank-you confirming the visit happened.
Endpoint: attendance completed (forum week of Jun 18–20, 2015; thank-you Jun 25, forwarded again Jul 31). Jun 20 session participation confirmed in advance (Jun 10, main 12843); Jun 18 session and plenary attendance NOT separately confirmed post-event (plenary confirmed in advance Jun 9, main 12704 — an advance confirmation, not a post-event record). The Lavrov meeting, Jun 19, was accepted TWICE in advance (Jun 15–16, main 11930); held/not-held NOT established. The Nabiullina meeting, Jun 19, was proposed with no acceptance in rows read. The Putin 1-1 was affirmatively CANCELLED Jun 8, 2015 (main 11930 — Belyakov: "This year we won't be able to make the 1-1 session"), not merely unconfirmed. The RDIF/Russia 24 teledebate, Jun 19, was an invitation only (main 12054; Barak not among the listed panelists). The Open Innovations Forum keynote invitation, Moscow, Oct 28–Nov 1, 2015, is now CHECKED: "Open Innovations" scores 2 hits in all five DBs combined, both the invitation itself (main 12310 and main 8321); attendance NOT established. Extends fragment F1 (Sochi/Ushakov, Dec 2013–Feb 2014) — the Ushakov link is the prior-access arrangement, not the 2015 event. in full. Confirmed for the attendance leg only; meeting/plenary legs

v3.2 (WS3) extension — main-DB follow-up (all anchors body-read in full): plenary — confirmed in advance, Jun 9, 2015 (main 12704, Nili→Kartasheva: "Former PM Barak will participate at the plenary session." Flights: arrival Wed Jun 17, 18:15, SU 6268 Tel Aviv→St. Petersburg; departure Sun Jun 21, 15:55, BA 879 to London; Kempinski Hotel; security detail arriving Jun 15). This is an advance confirmation to the organizer, not a post-event record; post-event plenary attendance is still NOT separately confirmed in rows read — the Jun 25 thank-you (main 12310) confirms the visit as a whole, not the plenary sitting. Lavrov meeting, Jun 19 — proposed, accepted twice in advance; held/not-held NOT established (main 11930, Jun 8–16 chain: Jun 15, Belyakov: "Minister Sergey Lavrov would be glad to meet with you on June 19th 14:30 – 15:00. Would it work for you?" Barak: "It works. Of course." Jun 16, Belyakov: "Sergey Lavrov asked to move your meeting a little earlier, to 13:30 – 14:00 (pavilion 33, conference room 1). Would it be ok?" Barak, 17:27: "Thanks. It is Ok. I'll be there on time."). v3.2 (WS5) extension — Beliakov, the SPIEF organizer: EFTA00683972 (DS9, May 2, 2014): Olivier Colom → Epstein: "Sergey beliakov. He is the organiser of the Saint-Petersburg forum." Identifies Beliakov as the SPIEF organizer; pre-SPIEF contact. "Beliakov" is a Belyakov spelling variant not previously recorded. EFTA00334798 / EFTA00334818 (DS9, Nov 19, 2015): Groff → Beliakov, reconfirming a visit to Epstein's NY home that evening at 7pm; Beliakov confirms. EFTA00317690 / EFTA00317691 / EFTA00318469 / EFTA00318500 (DS9, Sep 22–Oct 6, 2016): Groff scheduling Beliakov's Oct 6, 2016 visit (4:30pm, 9 East 71st Street); Beliakov confirms; visit reconfirmed Oct 6. The remaining ~100 BELYAKOV docs are routine Groff schedule emails in which "Beliakov" appears in the calendar body — investigated, no chain. (EFTA00295176, a Sergey Beliakov vCard, and EFTA00461523, Oct 24, 2017, "Contact for the records", are contact-record notes, not legs.)

v3.3 (WS3) extension — the Apr 22, 2015 Barak–Belyakov meeting + the Beliakov contact record: **Span moves back to Apr 22, 2015.** Apr 23, 2015 — Epstein→Belyakov + Barak, subject "sergey – ehud" (main 10322; part02:1184 is the same message filed in part02 — a copy of main 10322, same content): Epstein's introduction email — the formal "sergey – ehud" handoff. Apr 23, 2015 — Belyakov to Barak (EFTA00628346, DS9; Barak's 19:54 reply quoting Belyakov's 15:41 message): **"It was a pleasure to make your acquaintance at the meeting yesterday, thank you and Jeffrey again. I sincerely hope you'll be able to attend SPIEF 2015. I think the Forum would benefit from your active participation in the program. My team will send you the official invitation next week. We'll also send you a list of people you might be interested in meeting with while in Saint Petersburg."** Barak replies the same evening: "Hi Sergey I'm trying to reach you over the phone and fail. I'll call you again in two hours." **The Barak–Belyakov meeting was held Apr 22, 2015** (Belyakov's own words, the day before this exchange); the formal invitation followed, as promised, on Apr 28 (part02:1161), which itself refers to "the 2 sessions which we discussed in NYC last week" — the Apr 22 meeting was in New York. Apr 16, 2015 — Groff→Epstein, subject "Ehud Barak (update)" (EFTA02337245, DS11): the scheduling record — **"Ehud will now come see you for dinner on Wed. April 22nd at 7pm (instead of lunch on 23rd). Wed. April 22, 2015 NY: 12:00pm Appt w/Sergey Beliakov, 7:00pm DINNER w/Ehud."** So Apr 22, 2015 in New York: Beliakov appointment at noon, dinner with Barak at 7pm — the meeting Belyakov thanks Barak for the next day was the noon appointment. Tier stays confirmed for the attendance leg only. The Beliakov contact record, 2014–2017 (minor legs, same precedent as v3.2 WS5): May 4, 2014 — completed meeting: Epstein→Beliakov, "fun" (EFTA02518712; copies EFTA02716999, EFTA02720114): **"I enjoyed our short meeting. If there is something I can do to help let me know. I hope to see you in New York. If you think wise I will send a staff member to attend your conference. Of course I will pay normal fees."** Two days after Colom's May 2, 2014 identification of Beliakov as the SPIEF organizer (EFTA00683972, already anchored); "your conference" is not named in the row. Jul 14, 2014 — call proposed: "Sergey Beliakov just called me (he is in Brazil for the summit). He would like to talk to you tmw. Around this time (9.30 ny time)." (EFTA02585722; follow-ups EFTA01748708 / EFTA01803880 / EFTA01918274 — scheduling only; the call itself is not confirmed in rows read). Jan 17–23, 2017 — meeting scheduled: EFTA02663012 (Jan 17: "Sergey Beliakov can meet on Monday or Tuesday."); EFTA02354457 (Jan 20: "Shall I confirm the meeting with sergey Beliakov on Monday?"); EFTA02341585 (Jan 23, 08:26: "Ok, meeting Sergey Beliakov today. Will call after that!"); DS9 copy EFTA00630749; EFTA01056297 (Jan 20: "confrim, not sure yet about travel"). Same-day scheduling, not a post-event record — held/not-held NOT established. Oct 24–25, 2017 — visit scheduled, appointment confirmed in advance: EFTA02365473 (Oct 24: "Will be in NYC October 25 evening till 29 morning. Will you have Time to see him?"); EFTA02353114 (Oct 24: Beliakov "asking if you could meet later as he is landing a= 520pm!", Epstein: "evenbing 25"); EFTA02227521 (Oct 24, 17:37: "830pm October 25th confirmed Sergey Beliakov"); EFTA02228152 (Oct 25, 20:54 schedule: "8:30pm Appt w/Sergey Beliakov and Yulia, his wife (he lands at 5:20pm)"); EFTA02228100 (calendar alert for the same 8:30pm Oct 25 appointment). Appointment confirmed in advance; held/not-held NOT established in rows read. This extends the Beliakov contact record to Oct 2017 — the latest Beliakov date in the corpus set. **Variant correction (WS3 §2.1):** the v3.2 entry's "'Beliakov' is a Belyakov spelling variant not previously recorded" stands as a variant note, but WS5 §2.3's "Beliakov — the dominant mailbox spelling of Belyakov (109 docs vs 58 for 'Belyakov')" is wrong as stated: measured across all five Barak DBs, the mailbox contains **Beliakov 0 times and Belyakov 109 times** (51 main + 10 part01 + 48 part02 — the 109 is the *Belyakov* mailbox count); the DOJ corpus contains **Beliakov 112 and Belyakov 59**. So **Beliakov is the dominant *DOJ-side* spelling; Belyakov is the *mailbox* spelling.** The variant list records both spellings with their populations. "Barok": mailbox 0 / corpus 6 / HO 0. "Barack" in the mailbox (v3.4 WS3, triaged in full): 317 rows — 309 Obama, 8 rows = 4 distinct "Barack"-for-Barak messages. "Barack"-for-Barak is now attested in five distinct instances: Shilin's "Dear Mr. Barack" (Jun 11, 2013, main 1155/24058, in P47); Colom's "Ehud Barack" via Epstein (Jul 5, 2013, main 23854/24025/1234); Epstein's own "ehud barack" (EFTA00639227, Sep 12, 2013, passing mention, no chain); Barak's dictation-machine sign-off "Love best Barack" (Sep 21, 2015, main 9611); Valori's "Ehud BARACK" (Dec 29, 2015, main 6333 = hyperion 206, canonical duplicates). The spelling arises in typed mail (Shilin, Colom, Valori) and in dictation output (Barak's own message). Cross-reference: P47 (the Ushakov story) carries the Jun 2015 SPIEF Putin-request leg, which corroborates from Ushakov's office that no Putin meeting was arranged at SPIEF 2015 — consistent with main 11930's Jun 8, 2015 cancellation above.

stories.entry_markdown:
Span: Sept 25, 2008 – July 2009.
Anchors: EFTA02729730 (Sept 25, 2008, 27 pp. — Doe #1 and #2 move in the
CVRA case, 08-cv-80736, Doc 28, to unseal the non-prosecution agreement
provided to their attorneys under seal); EFTA02729255 (Jan 7, 2009, 42
pp. — in the separate civil case C.M.A. v. Epstein & Kellen, 08-80811,
Doc 33, filed under seal, Epstein and Kellen move for a stay, citing the
deferred-prosecution agreement's confidentiality clause); EFTA02729648
(Jun 4, 2009, 53 pp. — the Palm Beach Post moves to intervene in State v.
Epstein, Case Nos. 2006-CF9454 & 2008-9381CF, seeking access to the
sealed plea/sentence documents, arguing the parties failed to comply
with Florida's sealing requirements and that continued sealing is
pointless because the documents were discussed in open court);
EFTA02729494 (2009, 26 pp. — Epstein's 4th DCA reply, Case 4D09-2554,
arguing the NPA and addendum are confidential, not a public record, and
should remain sealed, invoking supremacy/comity and the federal court's
prior denials of disclosure; its own filing date not established in the
text read; latest internal reference is Marra's July 16, 2009 order);
EFTA02729535 (Jul 13, 2009, 21 pp. — counsel enters an appearance for
respondent B.B., non-party intervenor below, in the 4th DCA case).
Chain: Jun 12, 2009 — at the Marra hearing on Epstein's renewed motion
to stay the civil cases, Brad Edwards advises the court he filed the NPA
under seal in the CVRA case; Jun 25, 2009 — Epstein's counsel advises
Judge Colbath of that sealed filing (both hearings recounted in
EFTA02729494). Jul 6, 2009 — Judge Marra orders the NPA filed under seal
for in camera review; Jul 16, 2009 — Judge Marra denies the motion to
stay (both July orders cited in the appendix to EFTA02729494).
Endpoint / dated stopping point: July 2009 (reply citing Marra's July
16, 2009 order). Whether any document was unsealed is NOT established
in the cluster — no unsealing order or released NPA copy was found here.
Tier: probable. The chain is connected (one object — the sealed NPA/plea
records — across three dockets) and dated, but the outcome is
undocumented in the cluster and the reply's own filing date was not
established. Allegations/positions labeled: the Post's sealing arguments
are the Post's; Epstein's confidentiality arguments are Epstein's;
neither is adopted as a finding. Links: P1 (the Sept 2008 motion is a
CVRA-case filing), Story 1 (the sealed plea records), Story 2 (the NPA
under challenge). Fold-away noted: the Sept 2008 leg could be filed as a
P1 extension and the state-court legs as a Story 1 extension; the chain
is presented whole here because the object and the 2008–2009 window are
common.
Verification (v3.0, WS1): document-level verified — anchors read in full
or substantial part.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — opposition + press discovery + filing dates: ~Sep 2008 — "Respondent's Opposition to Victims' Motion to Unseal Non-Prosecution Agreement" (CVRA case 08-80736) (EFTA00204641, DS9, 7 pp., shared with P1): the NPA "was never filed in the instant case by the United States, either under seal or otherwise"; Aug 14, 2008 telephonic hearing; Aug 21, 2008 Order to Compel Production and Protective Order (DE 26) — petitioners shall not disclose the Agreement to third parties absent further court order; the government advised the court the Agreement had three parts: (1) Sep 2007 NPA, (2) Oct 2007 addendum, (3) a letter from the US Attorney to Epstein's attorneys suggesting a further modification; Epstein's attorneys contended the Agreement comprised only parts one and two. (EFTA00204638 is the shorter 3 pp. version of the same filing.) Sep 16–17, 2008 — Palm Beach Daily News (via counsel) discovered the NPA + addendum were filed under seal and asks the basis for sealing; USAO internal: "We have no obligation to seek its continued sealing… she is going to notify [the SAO] that he has yet to file the remainder of the Agreement and that the unsealing issue is between him/Epstein and the SAO's office." (EFTA00211919, DS9, 2 pp.) Jun 15, 2009 Palm Beach Post editorial "Unseal the Epstein deal" + state-court Motion to Make Court Records Confidential (EFTA00183935, DS9, 162 pp.): the NPA was "filed under seal in the court file on July 2, 2008" and the Addendum "filed under seal… on August 25, 2008"; sealed by Judge Pucillo Jun 30, 2008; motions to vacate/unseal by EW (May 15, 2009) and Palm Beach Post (Jun 1, 2009); intervention granted Jun 10, 2009. Either way the statement→advice handoff is NOT established, and P35's Feb 2016 $300,000 opening credit is NOT corroborated by the statement stratum. Text-layer note (v3.4 WS1, reconciled): the same-date/different-amount pattern recurs on **eight** further paired dates — Apr 4, 2017 (statement $300,000 vs advice $400,000; Apr 30, 2017 statement, PDF p.235, arithmetic closes exactly) plus Jul 14, 2016 ($125,000 vs $500,000); Dec 16, 2016 ($150,000 vs $200,000); Aug 21, 2017 ($150,000 vs $600,000); Dec 8, 2017 ($150,000 vs $300,000); Apr 19, 2018 ($100,000 vs $150,000); Oct 31, 2018 ($200,000 vs $400,000); Mar 7, 2019 ($800,000 vs $700,000). **Correction to the v3.3 flag: the statement figure is NOT smaller in each case — Mar 7, 2019's statement figure ($800,000) exceeds the advice ($700,000).** Statement-side monthly credit arithmetic closes in every pair month (Dec 2016 / Dec 2017 summary endings are OCR misreads resolved by the daily balances: 256,528.49 and 286,475.34). The different-accounts reading is strengthened; the same-movement-different-amounts reading is not excluded. All eight further pairs are page-image verified (v3.5 WS5): Apr 4, 2017 (statement $300,000, EFTA01670187 PDF p.235, stamped EFTA01670421; advice $400,000, EFTA01273155 PDF p.4, stamped EFTA01273158, IMAD 20170404 B1Q8383C 014160); Jul 14, 2016 ($125,000, p.196/EFTA01670382; $500,000, p.2/EFTA01273156, IMAD 20160714 B1Q8383C 016693); Dec 16, 2016 ($150,000, p.218/EFTA01670404; $200,000, p.3/EFTA01273157, IMAD 20161216 B1Q8383C 012496); Aug 21, 2017 ($150,000, p.252/EFTA01670438; $600,000, p.5/EFTA01273159, IMAD 20170821 B1Q8383C 006622); Dec 8, 2017 ($150,000, p.267/EFTA01670453; $300,000, p.6/EFTA01273160, IMAD 20171208 B1Q8383C 007791); Apr 19, 2018 ($100,000, p.287/EFTA01670473; $150,000, p.9/EFTA01273163, IMAD 20180419 B1Q8383C 012418); Oct 31, 2018 ($200,000, p.317/EFTA01670503; $400,000, p.11/EFTA01273165, IMAD 20181031 B1Q8383C 030377); Mar 7, 2019 ($800,000, p.339/EFTA01670525; $700,000, p.12/EFTA01273166, IMAD 20190307 B1Q8383C 015128). In every pair month the statement's monthly arithmetic closes exactly on the statement figure, and the Dec 2016 / Dec 2017 printed ending balances (256,528.49 / 286,475.34) confirm the text-layer OCR corrections at image level. The Apr 2018 month closes exactly (beginning balance 100,507.28 on the image, not 100,507.26 as the text layer read — the '$0.02' gap was an OCR artefact). Both figures in every pair are confirmed as printed, so the amount discrepancies are real discrepancies, not misreads — but which reading they support is still undecided, since the deciding account numbers are redacted on both sides of all nine pairs. v3.3 (WS4) extension — FEDWIRE parser re-check, corrected count (see changelog §3): the v3.2 "lower bound" flag is now resolved. WS3's parser regex `Fedwire (Debit|Credit)\b` required the literal words Debit/Credit. OCR renders "Fedwire Debit" as **"Fedwire Debt"** and as **"FedwIre Debt"** / **"Fedwlre Debit"**, so those lines were missed; "Fed Wire Credit" (spaced) anchors were also missed. The variant population (WS5 FEDWIRE group) is **201 NEW documents** (sets 9/10/11; disjoint from WS3's 1,632-doc population). Re-check: **165 "Fed Wire Credit" anchors, 0 NC-bearing lines, 0 LSJ lines.** Thirteen missed lines, all verified by segment read (amount + IMAD + VIA FIRSTBANK PR + NC: LSJ LLC on the same block), in 12 documents — all debits via FirstBank PR to LSJ LLC: EFTA01482375 (Apr 15, 2003, $5,000, "Fedwire Debt", IMAD 0415B1C1GCO7C004975); EFTA01482408 (Aug 05, $75,000, "Fedwire Debt", IMAD 0805B1OGC08C002941); EFTA01482493 (May 25, 2004, $10,000, "Fedwlre Debit", IMAD 0525810GCO8C00426…); EFTA01482527 (Sep 09, 2004, $10,000, "Fedwire Debt", IMAD 0909810GC08C004225); EFTA01482634 (Aug 26, $10,000, "Fedwire Debt", IMAD 082691OGC04C006167); EFTA01482665 (Dec 13, 2005, $13,000, "Fedwlre Debit", IMAD 1213610GC0…); EFTA01482695 (Mar 20, 2006, $18,000, "Fedwire Debt", IMAD 032081…); EFTA01482763 (Sep 25, $10,000, "Fedwire Debt", IMAD 0925B10GC06C006170); EFTA01482834 (May 25, 2007, $27,000 "Fedwire Debt" IMAD 0525B1OGCO3C002945 + $100,000 "FedwIre Debt" IMAD 0525810GC04C002948 — already a P40 anchor); EFTA01482359 (Feb 27, 2003, $50,000, "Fedwire Debt" — a second LSJ line that day beside a WS3-caught $10,000 line); EFTA01482697 (Mar 23, $50,000, "Fedwire Debt" — same doc/date as a WS3-caught $10,000 line); EFTA01656686 (Feb 27, $50,000, "Fedwlre Debit"). Two apparent extras, EFTA01482927 and EFTA01483020, were **false positives** — "Fed Wire Credit" anchors borrowing the next line's NC within the 500-char window; the underlying LSJ debit lines there were already in WS3's data — excluded. The recheck missed 0 WS3 lines. **Corrected totals (WS3's own rule — NC-named LSJ LLC lines, occurrences): 316 → 329 lines; 210 → 218 documents.** Eight of the 12 documents are new to WS3's set; EFTA01482359, EFTA01482697 and EFTA01656686 already held a caught NC line each. Total NC-line population (all counterparties): WS3's 1,761 occurrences → **1,852 genuine occurrences** (1,854 parser hits minus the 2 false positives). Outside-DS10 exact-FEDWIRE documents (81 corpus-wide): **0 LSJ lines.** The earliest missed line is 2/27/2003 and the latest is 2009 — all mid-span legs; span and endpoints unchanged by the count correction (the span move to Feb 23, 2012 above is the separate v3.2-tension fix). One more LSJ item, a wire instruction rather than a Fedwire statement line (NOT counted in the 329): EFTA01591979 — "Reference: LSJ - Inv # 7714-30", Jun 14, 2010, $3,485 to Kraus–Manning. **Not folded into the 329** (see fragments F-33-14/F-33-15): BEN: LSJ LLC lines ~200–260 (231 by the 500-char rule; 200 by the block-delimited rule) and A/C: LSJ, LLC lines 543–552, concentrated in the EFTA01526xxx–EFTA01528xxx statement block (134 docs; same account 739-110438, Feb 2003 onward). **RESOLVED in v3.4 (WS1 — see the v3.4 extension below):** the A/C-vs-NC fuzzy-IMAD dedup is resolved (mixed) — the A/C lines are ~40% duplicates of NC wires and ~60% additional distinct wires; BEN lines are distinct wires. The 329 stays defined by the NC rule; BEN and A/C lines are recorded as P40 extension strata, not folded into the count.

v3.4 (WS1) extension — A/C- and BEN-format strata, fuzzy-IMAD dedup RESOLVED (see changelog §12): the v3.3 "UNRESOLVED" flag is now resolved. Re-extraction over the full 1,833-doc FEDWIRE population (WS3 popA 1,632 ∪ WS4 variant 201, overlap 0) with the improved anchor regex ("Fedwire Debt" / "FedwIre" / "Fedwlre" / "Fed Wire Credit" / "FedvAre") yields 1,037 LSJ lines, all debits: NC 323 lines / 244 docs, A/C 533 lines / 139 docs, BEN 178 lines / 90 docs, bare 3 lines / 3 docs. Exact-IMAD overlap A/C∩NC is 28/441 distinct A/C IMADs (29/533 lines); fuzzy overlap (O→0, I/l→1) is 30/441 distinct (31/533 lines) — **IMAD OCR variants do NOT explain the gap**. Seqkey test (MMDD + last 6 of the fuzzy IMAD): NC 232 distinct, A/C 429, shared 191; union 470 seqkeys (453–470 allowing same-day 1-digit sequence variants as possible duplicates). A/C lines matched to NC by seqkey: 211/533 (39.6%); unmatched: 322/533 (281 with an IMAD + 41 with no IMAD). **Verdict: MIXED — the A/C lines are ~40% duplicates of NC wires and ~60% additional distinct wires.** The gross A/C count is NOT added to P40's 329 (the 329 stays defined by the NC rule, comparable across versions); the distinct-wire union NC∪A/C is 470 seqkeys vs NC-only 232. BEN lines are distinct wires: 121 distinct seqkeys, overlap with NC 1, with A/C 0; total LSJ-wire universe NC∪A/C∪BEN 590 seqkeys. Exemplars: A/C — EFTA01526002 (Feb 03, 2003, IMAD 0203B1QGC05C001057; no NC counterpart — no NC IMAD with prefix 0203 at all), EFTA01482402 (Jul 15, 2003, IMAD 0715B10GC07C003540; $70,000 by balance arithmetic $488,806.36 → $418,806.36), EFTA01482869 (Sep 18, 2007, IMAD 0918B1QGC05C005267); BEN — EFTA01482459 (Feb 23, IMAD 022381OGC01C002797), EFTA01482467 (Feb 23, IMAD 0223B10GCO5C002902). Same account 739-110438, same beneficiary LSJ LLC, same VIA FirstBank PR, same era Feb 2003 onward — this material extends P40, it does not form separate stories. The (date, amount) test is weak (A/C amounts mostly unavailable — 11/533 lines); the Levenshtein ≤2 same-MMDD test (188/441 distinct, 42.6%) over-matches same-day different wires and is not the verdict test. Year check: shared seqkeys year-agree 159, disagree 6 (doc-year only) — all 6 investigated and explained as year-attribution artifacts (multi-year bundle docs; Dec/Jan statement boundary; one header year mis-OCR'd 2003 for 2005), not true cross-year IMAD collisions. WS4's 13 missed lines: 12/12 (doc, MMDD) present in the NC set. My NC 323 vs WS4's 329 (6 short) is a date-key artifact on my side, not missed lines; the 329 count is not challenged.

The Jul 15, 2019 burst: four same-day incoming wires from Southern Trust Company Inc into four HBRK sub-accounts — $1,500,000 (ZORRO) + $1,000,000 (JEGE) + $1,000,000 (HYPERION) + $1,000,000 (NEPTUNE) = $4,500,000 on Jul 15, 2019 — nine days after Epstein's Jul 6, 2019 arrest. The timing is stated; nothing is inferred about who instructed the wires. The Jul 31, 2019 $1,000,000 from Southern Country International into NEPTUNE is a fifth post-arrest inbound, from the Story 10 Schwab-account entity.

No closure document in the set (no "ACCOUNT CLOSED" anywhere in the 917 DS10 statements). The TD production itself was stamped Aug 2020, so the Sep 2019 stop is a property of the statements produced, not of the production date.
Tier: probable. Documented openings + recurring dated funding + dated stopping point (same shape as P40/P41). Cautions: no "EPSTEIN" string appears in any of the five HBRK docs — the tie to the Epstein orbit is the sub-account labels (ZORRO, JEGE, HYPERION — entities already in the atlas) plus the Southern Trust and Southern Country International funding legs; HBRK Associates Inc itself is not characterised beyond the account holder as recorded; NEPTUNE, LLC is a new entity name — no document in this pass states what Neptune, LLC is; all five docs come from one TD Bank production, stamped Aug 2020 (single-production caveat, as with P35's single-bundle caveat).
